nodes.statement: Let B_2(Q) be the invertible upper-triangular 2x2 matrices over Q, T the diagonal matrices and N the unit upper-triangular matrices. Every invertible element factors uniquely as D * n with D in T and n in N, and conjugation of an element of N by an invertible element stays in N. torusProj preserves multiplication. On any vertex type with a root, a parent function fixing the root, and a natural depth function that is zero at the root and strictly decreases along parents off the root, and for invertible labels off the root, root-to-vertex transport multiplies labels on the left: T(root) = I and T(v) = U(v) * T(parent(v)). The stage-one field u_N(v) equals D(v) * n(v)^{-1} * D(v)^{-1}, lies in N, and equals [[1, -b(v)/d2(v)], [0, 1]]. Dressing a tree edge by u_N yields D(child) * D(parent)^{-1}. For every label g and every pair of vertices, torusProj(u_N(target) * g * u_N(source)^{-1}) equals torusProj(g). A further diagonal vertex field, multiplied on the left at the child and on the right by its inverse at the parent, leaves that dressed tree edge diagonal. The stage-two field u_T(v) = D(v)^{-1} satisfies u_T(v) * u_N(v) = T(v)^{-1}, and u_T(target) * (u_N(target) * g * u_N(source)^{-1}) * u_T(source)^{-1} equals T(target)^{-1} * g * T(source). That dressed label equals I if and only if g = T(target) * T(source)^{-1}. A vertex field that is invertible at every vertex, equals I at the root, and satisfies U(v) = g(v) * g(parent(v))^{-1} off the root, equals the rooted transport. The factorization identity fails on [[0, 1], [0, 1]]. Replacing the (2, 2) entry by 1 does not preserve the product of [[2, 1], [0, 3]] with itself. On any commutative ring R, for A : R -> R -> R, the operators (bA)(u, v, w) = -A(u, w) and (A smile A)(u, v, w) = A(u, v) * A(v, w) with (bK)(u,v,w,z) = -K(u,w,z) + K(u,v,z) satisfy b composed with b equal to 0, the Bianchi identity for K = bA + A smile A, and endpoint gauge covariance K(A^g) = g(u) * K(A) * g(w)^{-1} for supplied g and g_inv with g(x) * g_inv(x) = 1 at every x, writing g_inv as g^{-1}, when A^g(x, y) = g(x) * A(x, y) * g_inv(y). For A(0,1)=1, A(1,2)=1, A(0,2)=0, g(0)=1 and g(1)=2, the source-only expression (g(0)*A(0,1))*(g(1)*A(1,2)) - (g(0)*A(0,2)) is not equal to g(0)*(A(0,1)*A(1,2) - A(0,2)). The same values with g(2)=1 and g(1)^{-1}=1/2 satisfy the endpoint identity. The arithmetic comparison of 2 with 3 records that these integers differ. On the four-vertex tree with parents 0, 0, 0, 2, transport at vertex 3 equals U(3) * U(2).

nodes.bottleneck: Keep v rational and nonzero, and keep the hypercharge normalization (dossier Q = T_3 + Y, documentation Q = T_3 + Y/2) stated.

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.6-DOUBLET claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: For rational a, b, c, d, r with r != 0 and a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2 = r^2, the four real component identities of u(Phi)^dagger Phi = (0, r) hold; for a real doublet (phi_+, phi_0) on the circle of radius r the real dressing matrix has determinant 1, is orthogonal and maps the doublet to (0, r).
nodes.bottleneck: Unitarity and det = 1 of the complex u(Phi), the covariance u(g_L Phi) = g_L u(Phi), and SU(2)_L invariance of the dressed W are not in Lean or Python.

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.6-WEINBERG claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: For rational g, g', v with g^2 + g'^2 != 0: sin^2 + cos^2 = 1, P_gamma + P_Z = I_2, P_gamma P_Z = P_Z P_gamma = 0, both are idempotent and M^2_neutral P_gamma = 0; if also g != 0 and v != 0 then M_W^2 / (M_Z^2 cos^2 theta_W) = 1.
nodes.bottleneck: M_Z^2 as the nonzero eigenvalue and the tree-level reading of rho are definitions in the file, not derived from a Lagrangian.

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.6-ANOMALY claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: With Y_Q = 1/6, Y_u = 2/3, Y_d = -1/3, Y_L = -1/2, Y_e = -1 and rational N_c: N_c(2Y_Q - Y_u - Y_d) = 0, the gravitational trace is 0, N_c Y_Q + Y_L = (N_c - 3)/6 and the cubic trace is (3 - N_c)/4, so each of the last two vanishes iff N_c = 3.
nodes.bottleneck: These are polynomial identities over Q, not triangle-diagram anomaly computations; the dossier prints the cubic trace as (3/4)(3 - N_c) and the change log as 6 A_grav = 6(N_c - 3), both inconsistent with Lean, which is retained.

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.6-FENCE claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status OPEN
nodes.statement: For every z in Q(i) and every doublet Phi in Q(i)^2, the un-normalized dressing U(Phi) = [[conj phi2, phi1], [-conj phi1, phi2]] satisfies U(z Phi) = U(Phi) diag(conj z, z). When the squared modulus of z is 1 and a rational s with s*s equal to the squared norm of Phi is supplied, dividing every entry by that same s preserves the identity and s*s equals the squared norm of z Phi. On Phi = (1, 0), the unit z = 3/5 + (4/5)i with s = 1 has normalized (1, 2) entry 3/5 + (4/5)i. On the same Phi, z = 2 has squared norms 1 and 4; dividing by the respective rational roots 1 and 2 makes the normalized (1, 2) entries 1 and 2, so they differ. Continuum phases, the dressed derivative term, and an electroweak reading without a declared rational square root stay unproved.
imported_structure: continuum gauge fields W_mu and derivatives
U(1)_Y phases outside Q(i)
nodes.bottleneck: The normalized residual law is recorded when z lies in Q(i), the squared modulus of z is 1, and a rational s with s*s equal to the doublet squared norm is supplied. Continuum gauge fields W_mu, derivatives, phases outside Q(i), and the Elitzur or symmetry-breaking reading stay open.

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.7-DEF claims DEFINITION; audited status DEFINITION
nodes.statement: K_{N_g,N_g} has N_g up and N_g down vertices and N_g^2 edges carrying V_{alpha j}; rephasing V_{alpha j} -> e^{i phi_alpha} V_{alpha j} e^{-i phi_j} is a U(1) vertex coboundary, and the plaquette is Q_{alpha beta j k}(V) = V_{alpha j} V_{beta k} conj(V_{alpha k}) conj(V_{beta j}).
nodes.bottleneck: Keep the phases in the unit circle of Q(i) or declare the larger field.

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.7-COUNT claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: For every rational n, n^2 - (2n - 1) = (n - 1)^2, and (n - 1)(n - 2)/2 equals 0, 0, 1, 3 at n = 1, 2, 3, 4.
nodes.bottleneck: That a spanning tree of K_{n,n} has 2n - 1 edges and that unitarity reduces the (n-1)^2 cycle phases to (n-1)(n-2)/2 CP phases are cited, not formalized.

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.7-QUARTET claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: For Gaussian rationals with |u_i| = |d_j| = 1, rephasing row i by u_i preserves v_ij conj(v_il), rephasing column j by d_j preserves v_ij conj(v_kj), and the quartet Q(v_ij, v_kl, v_il, v_kj) is unchanged when its two row-i entries are rephased by u_i.
nodes.bottleneck: Invariance under the full U(1)^{N_g} x U(1)^{N_g} rephasing follows by composing single-vertex steps and is not written in Lean; Python checks all 9 plaquettes under one fixed rephasing.

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.7-TWO-GEN claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN

nodes.bottleneck: The physical reading (no CP phase for two generations) needs the full unitary 2x2 hypothesis set and the rephasing quotient.

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.7-THREE-GEN claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED
nodes.statement: For the fixed 3x3 Gaussian-rational matrix with c_i = 3/5, s_i = 4/5 and e^{i delta} = i, the three rows have unit norm, rows 1 and 2 are orthogonal, and the plaquette imaginary parts are +-5184/78125, nonzero.

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.7-FENCE claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status OPEN

measured CKM parameters

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.8-DEF claims DEFINITION; audited status DEFINITION
nodes.statement: On a finite graph with SU(3, Q(i)) links, the discrete Landau condition is the vanishing vertex divergence of the traceless anti-Hermitian parts of U^g; K_4 = {I, diag(1,-1,-1), diag(-1,1,-1), diag(-1,-1,1)}; the Hessian form along H^(23) = E_23 + E_32 is Tr(U (H^(23))^2).
nodes.bottleneck: The quadratic form along one generator is a stand-in for the Faddeev-Popov operator, not its spectrum.

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.8-GRIBOV claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED
nodes.statement: On the diamond graph, the 64 anchored maps V -> K_4 applied to the trivial connection give 64 configurations (63 nontrivial) with Hermitian links, hence zero discrete Landau divergence; some link has trace -1 and Tr(U (H^(23))^2) = -2 versus +2 at the identity; dressing along one fixed tree sends all 64 to the trivial configuration.
nodes.bottleneck: The collapse holds because every copy is pure gauge; the check does not compare dressing with Landau gauge on configurations with nonzero curvature.

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.8-SU3 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED
nodes.statement: On the diamond graph with five fixed non-commuting Pythagorean SU(3, Q(i)) links and one anchored SU(3, Q(i)) vertex gauge, for each of the 8 spanning trees the dressing sets tree links to I_3 and the dressed configuration is gauge-unchanged.
nodes.bottleneck: The statement for every group and graph is the specialization of TFQ-0398 and TFQ-0399 (root-fixing gauges leave residuals unchanged); continuum uniqueness is not claimed.

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.8-FENCE claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status OPEN

Faddeev-Popov quantization

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.9-DEF claims DEFINITION; audited status DEFINITION
nodes.statement: Lambda(beta) for rational beta in (-1, 1) is the boost with entries (1+beta^2)/(1-beta^2) and 2 beta/(1-beta^2); each 4-simplex carries e_sigma in GL(4, Q), each shared tetrahedron Omega in SO+(1,3; Q); g_sigma = e^T eta e, Gamma = e_sigma^{-1} Omega e_sigma', and H_h is the ordered product of Gamma around a hinge.

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.9-BOOST claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: For rational beta with 1 - beta^2 != 0, the 2x2 boost-plane matrix Lambda(beta) has determinant 1, Lambda(beta) Lambda(-beta) = I, Lambda^T eta_2 Lambda = eta_2, and e^T eta_2 e is unchanged when the 2x2 frame e is replaced by Lambda(-beta) e.

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.9-TRANSPORT claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_PROSE

nodes.source_status: papers/ravera_dfm_dossier.md record DFM-P3.9-HINGE claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED
nodes.statement: A telescoping product of pure-gauge frame factors is I_4; Lambda(1/2) Lambda(1/3) Lambda(-1/3) has 4x4 trace 16/3 (boost-plane trace 10/3) and the same trace after tetrad conjugation; the product of three telescoping conjugated factors around a declared 3-cell is I_4.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-DEF-PARITY-SCHEDULE claims DEFINITION; audited status DEFINITION
nodes.statement: A parity schedule is a declared finite cochain complex C0 -d0-> C1 -d1-> C2 over F2 given by binary incidence matrices with d1 d0 = 0 mod 2; C0 holds vertex gauge flips, C1 edge parity residuals, C2 plaquette syndromes.
imported_structure: declared incidence matrices d0, d1 over F2
nodes.bottleneck: The complex and its incidence matrices are declared inputs; nothing here derives them from a device or from the trunk window.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-DEF-TRICHOTOMY-LABELS claims DEFINITION; audited status DEFINITION
nodes.statement: For a residual w in C1: Exact means w = d0 a for some a in C0; ClosedResidual means d1 w = 0 and w is not Exact; OpenObstruction means d1 w is nonzero.
nodes.bottleneck: These are diagnostic schedule classes only; their relation to FOC terminals is fenced by TFQ-0181.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-DEF-PHI1-F2 claims DEFINITION; audited status DEFINITION
nodes.statement: H1 = ker d1 / im d0 over F2, and the quotient residual mass of a class is Phi1([r]) = min over a in C0 of wt(r + d0 a), the Hamming weight of a lightest coset representative.
nodes.bottleneck: This is the unit-weight binary specialization of the trunk Phi1 quotient seminorm; the coefficient change from weighted l1 to F2 Hamming weight is declared, not derived.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-C2 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: For every declared F2 cochain complex (with d1 d0 = 0 as a structure field) every Exact residual is a cocycle, and no residual satisfies two of Exact, ClosedResidual and OpenObstruction.
nodes.bottleneck: Exhaustiveness (each residual has at least one label) is not stated in Lean; it is the prose record MAJ-THM-TRICHOTOMY-EXHAUSTIVE.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-THM-TRICHOTOMY-EXHAUSTIVE claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_PROSE
nodes.statement: Since im d0 is contained in ker d1, C1 is the disjoint union of im d0, ker d1 minus im d0, and C1 minus ker d1, so each residual carries exactly one of the three labels.
nodes.bottleneck: A Lean exhaustiveness lemma (a classical case split on d1 w = 0 and on membership in im d0) is absent from MajoranaCore.lean.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-C3 claims COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED; audited status PROVED_PROSE
nodes.statement: Given d0, d1 and w over F2, compute s = d1 w (OpenObstruction if s is nonzero), otherwise solve d0 a = w by Gaussian elimination (Exact if solvable, ClosedResidual if not); this uses polynomially many bit operations, O(E (V + F)^2) by the body's count.
nodes.bottleneck: No Lean statement of the algorithm or its operation count exists; gaussian_elimination_cubic_bound is a reflexivity and must not be cited for this theorem.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-C4 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status DEFINITION
nodes.statement: If the declared matrices have d1 d0 nonzero mod 2 (or a residual of the wrong length is supplied), the evaluator emits RepresentationInvalid and assigns no residual class.
nodes.bottleneck: The refusal is a rule of the procedure; the Lean lemma only records that a violating vector falsifies the nilpotency predicate.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-EX-TORUS-2X2 claims PROVED_PROSE; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-C11 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-THM-SYNDROME-RECOVERY claims PROVED_PROSE; audited status PROVED_PROSE
nodes.statement: For B = im d0, Q = d1 and an admitted error set E in C1, a syndrome-only recovery succeeds for every e in E if and only if (E + E) intersected with ker Q is contained in B.
imported_structure: recovery model: deterministic syndrome-only decoder applying a C1 correction; success means the residual error lies in B
nodes.bottleneck: Lean or exact-code witness of the criterion is absent; the recovery model (deterministic decoder seeing only Qe, success meaning the residual lies in B) is declared in the proof.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-COR-DISTANCE-WEIGHT claims PROVED_PROSE; audited status OPEN
nodes.statement: With d = min{wt(z) : z in ker Q minus B}, the weight-bounded set E_t = {e : wt(e) <= t} satisfies the recovery criterion if and only if 2t < d.
imported_structure: Knill-Laflamme conditions P Ea^dagger Eb P = c_ab P (cited for general channels)
nodes.bottleneck: Write the two-direction weight argument from Theorem 4.4 (sum of two weight-t errors has weight at most 2t; a weight-d logical splits into two weight-at-most-t halves when d <= 2t); the Knill-Laflamme correspondence is cited, not derived.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-OPEN-LOCALITY-VIABILITY claims OPEN; audited status OPEN

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-C5 claims DEFINITION; audited status DEFINITION

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-DEF-TETRON-CARRIER claims DEFINITION; audited status DEFINITION

nodes.statement: On the 3x4 tetron torus (12 sites, 24 channels, 12 islands) exhaustive Gray-code coset search gives Phi1 = 3 for the column class, 4 for the row class and 7 for their sum, all ClosedResidual, so the distance of that instance is 3.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-COMP-BUDGET-CAP claims COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-C16 claims COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED

nodes.bottleneck: A validated realization map from a device to a declared complex is not supplied by this source.

nodes.statement: A measurement projection M is DETECTOR_INADEQUATE for a hypothesis pair when two distinct candidate states have the same readout (rho1 - rho2 in ker M), so the protocol cannot discriminate them.
nodes.bottleneck: Which laboratory maps M are adequate is the open program MAJ-OPEN-EVIDENCE-ADEQUACY.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-C10 claims DEFINITION; audited status DEFINITION
nodes.statement: Device baths, continuum BdG spectra, fabrication narratives, conductance peaks 2e^2/h, gap protocols and capacitance shifts C_Q are external observer projections: they may motivate which complex to declare but do not populate F2 receipts or mint authority without a validated realization map.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/majorana/the_majorana_problem.md record MAJ-C18 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status OPEN
nodes.statement: For four MZMs under a Lindblad braiding model with gap Delta, length L/xi and poisoning rate Gamma_qp > 0, the trace-norm transfer defect obeys Delta_transfer(T) <= min(1, C_LZ (hbar/(Delta T))^2 + (Delta/hbar) e^{-L/xi} T + 1 - e^{-Gamma_qp T}) for T >> hbar/Delta, and that envelope has a positive minimum.
imported_structure: Lindblad master equation with poisoning and dephasing channels
Landau-Zener leakage asymptotics

nodes.bottleneck: Derive the bath term A_s T^p and p(s) from the spectral density; the calculus minimization of the stated envelope is not written out.

exponential overlap splitting delta E_ij

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-018 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_PROSE
nodes.statement: On an admitted N-dimensional complex inner-product space V with orthonormal basis e_i, creation c_i^dagger = e_i wedge - and interior annihilation c_i on the exterior algebra of V (dimension 2^N) satisfy {c_i, c_j} = 0 and {c_i, c_j^dagger} = delta_ij; in particular (c_i)^2 = 0.
imported_structure: complex mode space V with inner product (admitted)
exterior Fock space as the carrier for fermionic states (admitted)
nodes.bottleneck: Mechanize the CAR identities on the exterior algebra; the statistics choice (exterior versus symmetric algebra) is an admitted postulate, and identifying modes with spin-1/2 particles needs the relativistic spin-statistics theorem, outside this finite setting.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-019 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED
nodes.statement: In the increasing occupation ordering on 6 modes, the sign of the hop c_target^dagger c_source on every occupation bitmask equals the product of the Jordan-Wigner parities of the annihilation and the creation step, checked exhaustively over all 2^6 states and ordered mode pairs.
imported_structure: Jordan-Wigner mapping between spin-1/2 Pauli operators and CAR operators (standard literature result)
nodes.bottleneck: The general Jordan-Wigner bijection c_j = (prod_{k<j} -sigma^z_k) sigma^-_j between spin-1/2 chains and CAR operators is a standard result imported here, not derived or mechanized in this checkout.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-020 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION
nodes.statement: For N CAR modes, gamma_{2j-1} = c_j + c_j^dagger and gamma_{2j} = -i(c_j - c_j^dagger) are self-adjoint with {gamma_a, gamma_b} = 2 delta_ab, generate the Clifford algebra on 2N generators, and P = prod_j (-i gamma_{2j-1} gamma_{2j}) is the fermion parity (-1)^N_op.
imported_structure: Majorana operator decomposition of CAR modes (standard literature result)
fermion parity superselection (physical postulate)
nodes.bottleneck: Standard algebra imported, not derived here; the trunk mechanizes only the two-generator case (DS-QM212-MAJORANA-PROBLEM). Parity superselection is a physical postulate, not a consequence of the algebra.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-021 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_PROSE
nodes.statement: The CAR constrain the operators c_i, not the Hamiltonian: H = 0, free hopping -t sum c_i^dagger c_j and the Hubbard H(t, U) are distinct Hermitian number-conserving operators on the same CAR Fock space, so a physical Hamiltonian is an added admission (explicit 2-site Hubbard matrix computed by hand).
imported_structure: Hermitian Hamiltonian H = H^dagger (admitted)
particle-number conservation [H, N] = 0 (admitted)
locality graph and real hopping t (admitted)
Hubbard on-site interaction U (admitted)
nodes.bottleneck: Hermiticity, number conservation, a locality graph, a one- and two-body truncation and the interaction U remain explicit admissions in every downstream sign record.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-022 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_PROSE
nodes.statement: For a finite self-adjoint H with H_xx = V_x, H_xy = -a_xy (-1)^{eps_xy} (a_xy > 0, eps symmetric), beta >= 0 and E* >= max V_x, Z = e^{-beta E*} sum_m beta^m/m! sum over closed length-m configuration paths of prod K_{x_{j+1} x_j} with K = E* I - H, and each nonzero closed term has sign (-1)^{sum of eps along the path}.
imported_structure: positive edge magnitudes a_xy, parities eps_xy and diagonal energies V_x on an orthonormal configuration basis (supplied; ledger ORIGIN-001)
nodes.bottleneck: The sign of a closed term is a property of the supplied magnitudes, parities and representation; vertex sign gauges remove all negative entries exactly when every configuration cycle is even (FSP-SWITCHING-NORMAL-FORM). Trotter slicing and its error are separate.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-023 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status DEFINITION
nodes.statement: For a declared path representation with weights W(c), <Sign> = Z / Z_abs with Z = sum sigma(c)|W(c)| and Z_abs = sum |W(c)|; when Z > 0, Delta f := -(1/(beta N)) log <Sign> >= 0, so <Sign> = exp(-beta N Delta f) holds by definition.
imported_structure: declared path representation (basis and operator expansion)
nodes.bottleneck: Exponential decay in beta N is a hypothesis (Delta f bounded below by a positive constant uniformly in N and beta), not a theorem; Z_abs is an operational absolute ensemble, not in general a physical bosonic system.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-024 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_PROSE
nodes.statement: For M_s independent samples from |W|/Z_abs, the sign mean has variance (1 - <Sign>^2)/M_s, so relative error epsilon needs M_s >= (1 - <Sign>^2)/(epsilon^2 <Sign>^2); if <Sign> = exp(-beta N Delta f) this is Omega(exp(2 beta N Delta f)).
imported_structure: independent sampling from the absolute-weight distribution (assumption)
nodes.bottleneck: Correlated Markov-chain samples, observable numerators and the extensive-gap hypothesis need separate treatment; this bound concerns direct reweighting only, not every estimator or representation.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-025 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED
nodes.statement: For the 3-site spinless triangle, t = 1, U = 0, two fermions, beta = 2 and three Euler slices, the occupation-basis expansion has 27 paths, 6 negative of weight 8/27 and positive weights in {4/9, 1}, so no equal-weight pairing exists there; in the one-body eigenbasis H is diagonal with E in {-1, -1, 2} and Z = 2e^2 + e^-4.
nodes.bottleneck: Frustration alone does not imply disjoint weight spectra or hardness (ledger GIN-C4, INV-DISJOINT-SPEC); the general Lean lemma covers only the step from disjoint spectra to no weight-preserving sign-reversing involution.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-026 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION
nodes.statement: Troyer-Wiese (2005): the NP-complete decision whether a 3D +-J Ising spin glass has ground energy below a threshold reduces in polynomial time to estimating the thermal energy of the frustrated quantum model -sum J_ij sigma^x_i sigma^x_j at beta J >= N ln 2 + ln(12N); a deterministic polynomial estimator for that family would give P = NP, a randomized one NP subset of BPP.
imported_structure: Troyer and Wiese, PRL 94, 170201 (2005), cond-mat/0408370, equations (10)-(11) and footnote 9
NP-completeness of the 3D Ising spin-glass ground-state decision problem (Barahona)
nodes.bottleneck: This is a worst-case statement about a model family under a precision promise; it is not formalized here, is not a reduction to the Hubbard model, and does not make any fixed finite system or every fermionic Hamiltonian intractable.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-027 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: For any carrier with weights in N and signs +-1, an involution tau with w(tau c) = w(c) and sign(tau c) = -sign(c) has no fixed point and each pair satisfies w(c) sign(c) + w(tau c) sign(tau c) = 0; zero signed sum does not require such a pairing (+2, -1, -1), and a cancelling doublet can carry a nonzero observable numerator.
imported_structure: supplied weight-preserving sign-reversing involution
nodes.bottleneck: Summing pairs to get sum_c w(c) sign(c) = 0 on a finite set is a prose orbit-partition step (manuscript Section 4.2), not mechanized; observable numerators need A o tau = A; the involution is sufficient, not necessary (INV-INVOL-CANC).

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-029 claims COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED; audited status COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED
nodes.statement: For the four-site periodic ring, U = 0, two spin-up fermions, beta = 3/2 and four Euler slices, all 32 negative Euler-transfer paths are matched to disjoint positive paths of exactly equal rational weight within one weight fiber, and a posting-list query over k modes uses k posting-list operations.
nodes.bottleneck: Pairing is on exact weight fibers of enumerated paths, not a spectator-preserving symmetry (INV-GIN-PARITY); it does not preserve general observables, and path enumeration grows exponentially. CT-AUX update stability for multi-orbital models has no evidence here.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-030 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_PROSE
nodes.statement: For d0 in Q^{m x n} and W = im d0, N_W(x) = x - sum_i x_{p_i} r_i (nonzero RREF rows r_i of d0^T with pivots p_i) is sound, idempotent and complete for x ~ y iff x - y in W, and is independent of the generating matrix; Lean checks the three laws for the fixed integral image span(1, 2) in Z^2.
imported_structure: fixed rational coboundary matrix d0 and coordinate order
nodes.bottleneck: N_W is not an l1 minimizer (span(1,2), x = (1,0) gives norm 2 versus 1); the quotient norm is a separate exact linear program with a refusal budget (NF-003). A valid YAML contract or routing label is not a normalizer.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-032 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-033 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION
nodes.statement: The Wilson-Dirac operator satisfies gamma5 D_W gamma5 = D_W^dagger, so its nonreal eigenvalues come in conjugate pairs and det D_W is real; for two degenerate flavors det(D_W)^2 >= 0.
imported_structure: Wilson-Dirac lattice fermion operator with r = 1 (standard lattice QCD)
nodes.bottleneck: A single-flavor det D_W can be negative; the JSONL claim that det D_W is nonnegative is only the two-flavor square. The gamma5 adjoint, reality of det D_W, and the two-flavor square for this operator are not Lean theorems in this checkout. Euclidean Clifford data in dimensions 2 and 4 are checked in Lean. An exact check on one periodic 2x2 lattice, mass -1, U(1), finds det = -3.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-034 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION
nodes.statement: Adding S_theta = i theta Q_top with real lattice charge Q_top multiplies the Boltzmann weight by exp(-i theta Q_top), which is nonreal unless theta Q_top lies in pi Z for every configuration, so positive-weight importance sampling is lost for generic theta != 0.
imported_structure: lattice topological charge Q_top and theta vacuum term (standard)
nodes.bottleneck: Severity of the resulting sign problem is phenomenology from the literature; the checkout has no theta-term model.

nodes.source_status: papers/core/fsp/theory_of_finite_fsp.jsonl record FSP-DERIV-035 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status OPEN
nodes.statement: Target: on a finite slab lattice the chiral variation of the boundary fermion determinant cancels the bulk Chern-Simons variation. Not established in this checkout. One tested candidate does not realize it, as expected: on open Wilson slabs with U(1) links, the gauge change acts on the Wilson matrix by a diagonal similarity, so the full, interior, boundary Schur and fixed site-matched chiral-block determinants are gauge invariant by construction, while a lifted cup-product CS term whose coefficient is not derived from the fermions changes by 1/32. This is a fixed-basis truncation of a vector-like regulator, not an obstruction to lattice inflow.
imported_structure: Callan-Harvey continuum anomaly inflow (literature)
nodes.bottleneck: Construct a regulated chiral boundary determinant whose projector, basis or measure depends on the gauge field (domain-wall or overlap/Ginsparg-Wilson type), derive from the same fermions the bulk Chern-Simons term they induce, and show that the two gauge variations cancel. The fixed-basis Wilson-slab test cannot register an anomaly, because site-matched fixed bases give similarity-invariant determinants; its bare lifted CS candidate is neither induced by the fermions nor well defined on U(1) links (an integer lift of the same links changes it by 1/8). The continuum Callan-Harvey mechanism remains a literature import.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-Q0 claims OPEN; audited status OPEN
nodes.statement: Every step of a noisy quantum computation, syndrome extraction and repair included, adds residual, and repair consumes capacity while adding residual of its own; the question is whether this makes reliable completion a self-referential no-go or a threshold condition that holds only under named resource assumptions (fresh supply, net-efficient repair, bounded overhead growth, physical error below threshold).
nodes.bottleneck: The finite model answers the question as a threshold condition (QCV-Q1 to QCV-Q6); whether any physical system meets the named assumptions is not derived and no verdict on physical viability is given.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-Q1 claims DEFINITION; audited status DEFINITION
nodes.statement: Backlog q(t+1) = max(0, q(t) + lam + g*mu - mu) in units of the Phi_1 repair cost, where lam is the residual generated per round by the computation, mu = kappa*r the repair rate from r fresh ancillas per round at kappa units each, and g the residual generated per unit of repair; with g = 0 this is the DS-QM101 queue; a distance-three level with a fault locations has constant c = a(a-1)/2.
imported_structure: declared generation rate lam
declared self-generated fraction g of repair
declared capacity kappa per fresh ancilla
declared fresh supply r per round
nodes.bottleneck: lam, g, kappa and r are declared inputs; no value is derived or measured for any code, and Phi_1 of a residual is not computed here.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-Q1B claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: In the QCV-Q1 model with q0 >= 0, the backlog is bounded iff lam <= (1-g)*mu; for g >= 1 and lam > 0 no mu >= 0 bounds it; for g < 1 and mu = kappa*r, with kappa > 0, it is bounded iff r >= lam/((1-g)*kappa); with r = 0 and lam > 0 it equals q0 + t*lam.
nodes.bottleneck: A statement inside the declared model; it does not say any code has g < 1 or that any supply r is available.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-Q1C claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: The union-bound recurrence p(k+1) = a*p(k) with a >= 1 and p(0) > 0 does not tend to zero; for 2 <= a <= b fault locations the certified threshold 1/pairCount(b) is at most 1/pairCount(a).
nodes.bottleneck: The location counts are declared; nothing here says how many repair locations a physical code needs.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-IMP-THRESHOLD claims IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION
nodes.statement: The fault-tolerance threshold theorems (Shor 1996; Aharonov and Ben-Or 1997; Kitaev 1997; Knill, Laflamme and Zurek 1998; Aliferis, Gottesman and Preskill 2006) are cited under each theorem's own noise, locality and overhead hypotheses; they are not re-proved.
imported_structure: threshold theorems for concatenated codes under their stated noise models
nodes.bottleneck: Exact constants and noise hypotheses of each theorem are not reproduced; the finite recurrence in QCV-Q2 is the only part checked.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-Q2 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: For the recurrence p(k+1) = c*p(k)^2 over Q, c*p(k) = (c*p(0))^(2^k); for c > 0 and p(0) >= 0: if c*p(0) < 1 then p(k) tends to zero with c*p(k) <= (c*p(0))^(k+1) and, for c*p(0) <= 1/2, p(k) <= (1/2)^(2^k)/c; if c*p(0) = 1 then p(k) = 1/c for all k; if c*p(0) > 1 then p(k) diverges; so p(k) tends to zero iff p(0) < 1/c.
nodes.bottleneck: The recurrence is the hypothesis; no noise model is shown to obey it and no constant c is computed for any code.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-Q3 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: For p(k+1) = c(k)*p(k)^2 with c(k) >= 0, p(k) = p(0)^(2^k)*amp(k) with amp(0) = 1, amp(k+1) = c(k)*amp(k)^2, and some p(0) > 0 has p(k) tending to zero iff some M > 0 has amp(k) <= M^(2^k) for all k; the criterion holds for c(k) <= C, for c(k) <= A*B^(k+1) with A, B >= 1, for c(k) = (k+1)^2, and for c(k) <= a*b^N(k) with block size N(k+1) <= s*N(k), s < 2; it fails for c(k) >= a*b^(2^k) with a > 0, b > 1, and for c(k) >= a*b^N(k) with 2^k <= N(k), b > 1, where no positive p(0) has p(k) tending to zero.
nodes.bottleneck: The families are exact illustrations of the criterion, not claims that any physical overhead has such a form; correlated-noise strength as an exponential of block size is a declared toy.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-IMP-ABIN claims IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION; audited status IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION
nodes.statement: Aharonov, Ben-Or, Impagliazzo and Nisan (1996) show that noisy reversible or quantum computation with no supply of fresh low-entropy bits cannot preserve its input beyond a short depth; the result is cited, not re-proved or imported as a proof here.
imported_structure: ABIN 1996 limitation theorem for noisy reversible computation
nodes.bottleneck: The exact statement and its noise model are in the cited paper; QCV-Q4 establishes a finite exact analogue for global depolarizing noise only.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-Q4 claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN
nodes.statement: For complex matrices of any size d and the variational trace norm tn(X) = sup over unitaries U of |tr(UX)|, the global depolarizing channel satisfies tn(Delta_p(rho) - Delta_p(sigma)) = (1-p)*tn(rho - sigma) for equal-trace rho, sigma and p <= 1; along any history of unitaries V(i) with depolarizing rates p(i) in [0,1], tn(run rho - run sigma) = (product of (1-p(i)))*tn(rho - sigma), which is at most (1-p)^t*tn(rho - sigma) when every p(i) >= p, and (1-p)^t <= 1/(1+p*t).
imported_structure: variational trace norm equals the Schatten-1 norm (Ky Fan, cited)
global depolarizing noise at a declared rate after every step
nodes.bottleneck: The trace norm is the variational form, whose equality with the sum of singular values is cited; the noise is global depolarizing with a declared rate per step, not independent per-qubit noise, and the statement is about histories without fresh resets.

nodes.source_status: dag/research/quantum_computation_self_obstruction.md record QCV-Q4B claims PROVED_LEAN; audited status PROVED_LEAN

nodes.bottleneck: The identification of the qubit trace norm with the Bloch distance uses the cited eigenvalue fact; Python and Rust replays are exact on declared instances only.

fresh ancillas at rate r

records.name: Hierarchical Borel dressing beyond the diamond control
records.summary: Let B_2(Q) be the invertible upper-triangular 2x2 matrices over Q, T the diagonal matrices and N the unit upper-triangular matrices. Every invertible element factors uniquely as D * n with D in T and n in N, and conjugation of an element of N by an invertible element stays in N. torusProj preserves multiplication. On any vertex type with a root, a parent function and a depth function that strictly decreases along parents, and for invertible labels off the root, root-to-vertex transport multiplies labels on the left: T(root) = I and T(v) = U(v) * T(parent(v)). The stage-one field u_N(v) equals D(v) * n(v)^{-1} * D(v)^{-1}, lies in N, and equals [[1, -b(v)/d2(v)], [0, 1]]. Dressing a tree edge by u_N yields D(child) * D(parent)^{-1}. For every label g and every pair of vertices, torusProj(u_N(target) * g * u_N(source)^{-1}) equals torusProj(g). A further diagonal vertex field, multiplied on the left at the child and on the right by its inverse at the parent, leaves that dressed tree edge diagonal. The stage-two field u_T(v) = D(v)^{-1} satisfies u_T(v) * u_N(v) = T(v)^{-1}, and u_T(target) * (u_N(target) * g * u_N(source)^{-1}) * u_T(source)^{-1} equals T(target)^{-1} * g * T(source). That dressed label equals I if and only if g = T(target) * T(source)^{-1}. A vertex field that is invertible at every vertex, equals I at the root, and satisfies U(v) = g(v) * g(parent(v))^{-1} off the root, equals the rooted transport. The factorization identity fails on [[0, 1], [0, 1]]. Replacing the (2, 2) entry by 1 does not preserve the product of [[2, 1], [0, 3]] with itself. On any commutative ring, the operators (bA)(u, v, w) = -A(u, w) and (A smile A)(u, v, w) = A(u, v) * A(v, w) satisfy b composed with b equal to 0, the Bianchi identity for K = bA + A smile A, and endpoint gauge covariance K(A^g) = g(u) * K(A) * g(w)^{-1} when A^g(x, y) = g(x) * A(x, y) * g(y)^{-1}. For A(0,1)=1, A(1,2)=1, A(0,2)=0, g(0)=1 and g(1)=2, the source-only expression (g(0)*A(0,1))*(g(1)*A(1,2)) - (g(0)*A(0,2)) is not equal to g(0)*(A(0,1)*A(1,2) - A(0,2)). The same values with g(2)=1 and g(1)^{-1}=1/2 satisfy the endpoint identity. The arithmetic comparison of 2 with 3 records that these integers differ. On the four-vertex tree with parents 0, 0, 0, 2, transport at vertex 3 equals U(3) * U(2).
records.obligation: The rooted tree, given by a parent function and a strictly decreasing depth, and the incidence cochain are supplied data. This statement does not construct a spanning tree from an arbitrary graph, does not identify an obstruction with a computed cohomology group, and does not build a 2-plaquette prism. Continuum gauge theory, color transport and smooth patching stay outside this statement.

records.name: Exact syndrome-recovery criterion for an admitted error set
records.summary: For B = im d0, Q = d1 and an admitted error set E in C1, a syndrome-only recovery succeeds for every e in E if and only if (E + E) intersected with ker Q is contained in B.
records.obligation: Lean or exact-code witness of the criterion is absent; the recovery model (deterministic decoder seeing only Qe, success meaning the residual lies in B) is declared in the proof.

records.name: Weight-t errors are recoverable iff 2t < d
records.summary: With d = min{wt(z) : z in ker Q minus B}, the weight-bounded set E_t = {e : wt(e) <= t} satisfies the recovery criterion if and only if 2t < d.
records.obligation: Write the two-direction weight argument from Theorem 4.4 (sum of two weight-t errors has weight at most 2t; a weight-d logical splits into two weight-at-most-t halves when d <= 2t); the Knill-Laflamme correspondence is cited, not derived.

records.name: Lieb-Robinson extension of syndrome detectability
records.summary: Which distinctions a local system can detect, preserve or repair within a specified time may admit a Lieb-Robinson quantitative extension supporting conditional statements on quantum computing viability.
records.obligation: No such bound is stated or derived; the source says the papers do not yet justify a general verdict.

records.name: Surface-code shadows are diagnostic schedules, not threshold proofs
records.summary: Multi-plaquette surface-code models and the FTQC dictionary (error to residual, correctable to Exact, logical to ClosedResidual, detectable to OpenObstruction, distance to declared distance) are diagnostic software schedules, not physical noise processes, threshold certificates or fault-tolerance proofs.
records.obligation: Any threshold or fault-tolerance theorem for a physical device remains outside this record.

records.name: Parameterized tetron-array carriers (disk, cylinder, torus)
records.summary: A rows x cols tetron array takes MZM sites as vertices on a (rows or rows+1) x (cols or cols+1) grid, nearest-neighbour channels as edges and the rows x cols islands as 2-cells, with no wrap (disk), column wrap (cylinder) or both wraps (torus).
records.obligation: A tetron here is a 2-cell of a declared combinatorial carrier under an idealized corner-shared layout, not a superconducting island.

records.name: Computed dim H1 = 0, 1, 2 on disk, cylinder and torus tetron arrays
records.summary: For sizes 2x2, 2x3, 3x3, 3x4, 4x4, 5x5, 6x6, 6x8 and 8x8, F2 row reduction gives dim H1 = (E - rank d1) - rank d0 = 0 (disk), 1 (cylinder), 2 (torus), agreeing with (2 if closed else 1) minus the Euler characteristic, with d1 d0 = 0.
records.obligation: Fixed sizes only; a closed-form proof for all rows and cols is absent.

records.name: Trivial H1 admits no ClosedResidual
records.summary: If every cocycle of a declared F2 cochain complex is exact, then no residual is ClosedResidual.
records.obligation: None for the lemma; its use on the legacy carrier needs the legacy dim H1 = 0 measurement (MAJ-C13).

records.name: Retraction of the legacy tetron carrier
records.summary: Given the recorded measurement that legacy tetron_carrier.py had dim H1 = 0 at T = 1..4, every closed residual on it was Exact, so its results support no statement about logical sectors and are superseded by the tetron-array family.
records.obligation: The legacy carrier and its dim H1 = 0 computation are not in this checkout; the hypothesis is a change-log record.

records.name: Per-class minimum weights 3, 4, 7 and distance 3 on the 3x4 torus
records.summary: On the 3x4 tetron torus (12 sites, 24 channels, 12 islands) exhaustive Gray-code coset search gives Phi1 = 3 for the column class, 4 for the row class and 7 for their sum, all ClosedResidual, so the distance of that instance is 3.
records.obligation: Fixed instance only; additivity and d = min(rows, cols) for other sizes are MAJ-CLAIM-DISTANCE-FAMILY.

records.name: Distance formulas for the tetron-array families
records.summary: For all sizes the torus distance is min(rows, cols), the cylinder distance is rows + 1, and the diagonal class weight is rows + cols.
records.obligation: Prove the distance formulas (e.g. by a cut argument on the dual grid); the source gives a one-sentence traversal argument for additivity only.

records.name: Coset-weight decoding is NP-hard for general binary codes
records.summary: Minimum-weight coset decoding of a binary linear code given by its matrix is NP-hard (Berlekamp, McEliece and van Tilborg 1978).
records.obligation: Literature result; no reduction is formalized or replayed here.

records.name: Computing Phi1 is coset-leader decoding of im d0
records.summary: Phi1([r]) is the coset-leader weight of r for the binary code im d0, so with d0 ranging over all binary matrices exact Phi1 inherits the imported NP-hardness; restricted families such as planar or toric incidence matrices may admit polynomial decoders.
records.obligation: The hardness rests on the import; the identification with coset decoding is definitional; what holds for graph-incidence d0 of declared cell complexes is not analysed.

records.name: Budget-capped coset search returns a flagged upper bound
records.summary: When 2^rank(d0) exceeds the declared budget the Gray-code search stops, returns the lightest weight found with exact = False, and the Rust terminal drops from TypedHarmonic to ClosedResidual; checked on the 3x4 torus (budget 4, capped weight >= exact weight) and the 4x4 torus (budget 16).
records.obligation: Fixed instances; the upper-bound property of any searched representative is immediate from the definition of the minimum.

records.name: 6x6 torus classification timing and budget overflow
records.summary: On the 6x6 tetron torus (V = 36, E = 72, dim H1 = 2, rank d0 = 35) a weight-one residual classifies OpenObstruction within a 100 ms test bound in Rust and Python, and the full coset 2^35 exceeds the 2^20 search budget.
records.obligation: The body's 17 ms figure is not recorded in this checkout; the timed residual exits at the syndrome step, so the elimination step is not timed; timing is machine-dependent.

records.name: L^p norms coincide with Hamming weight on binary carriers
records.summary: For v with entries in {0, 1} and p >= 1, the sum of |v_i|^p equals wt(v), so l1 and l2^2 coset minimizations over F2 have identical objectives and minimizers; dim H1 >= 2 gives distinct logical classes, not a norm gap.
records.obligation: The Lean declaration does not state this identity; a Lean lemma over p-th powers of 0/1 entries is absent.

records.name: The Majorana problem as a realization packet gap
records.summary: The Majorana problem is the gap between continuum open-system device narratives (nanowires, zero-bias peaks, interferometric parity readout) and declared finite algebraic schedules (F2 cochain homology, Ising matrices): neither discharges the verification conditions of the other without an explicit realization map.
records.obligation: A validated realization map from a device to a declared complex is not supplied by this source.

records.name: DETECTOR_INADEQUATE for a non-injective measurement map
records.summary: A measurement projection M is DETECTOR_INADEQUATE for a hypothesis pair when two distinct candidate states have the same readout (rho1 - rho2 in ker M), so the protocol cannot discriminate them.
records.obligation: Which laboratory maps M are adequate is the open program MAJ-OPEN-EVIDENCE-ADEQUACY.

records.name: Syndrome-only readout is inadequate on the 2x2 tetron torus
records.summary: On the 2x2 tetron torus the column and row logical representatives are distinct cochains with equal zero syndrome d1 w, so the readout M(w) = d1 w is DETECTOR_INADEQUATE for them.
records.obligation: Fixed instance; the adequacy of a syndrome-plus-class readout is asserted, not computed.

records.name: Hardware narratives are quarantined observer projections
records.summary: Device baths, continuum BdG spectra, fabrication narratives, conductance peaks 2e^2/h, gap protocols and capacitance shifts C_Q are external observer projections: they may motivate which complex to declare but do not populate F2 receipts or mint authority without a validated realization map.
records.obligation: A realization map that would lift this quarantine is not supplied.

records.name: Binding non-claims of the Majorana monograph
records.summary: The source makes no claim of physical MZM detection, vendor endorsement, FOC terminal identity, a generic FSP solution, a complete topological gate set from Ising braiding, an l1-vs-l2 separation over F2, unbounded exact syndrome decoding, physical tetron hardware, or falsity of external measurements.
records.obligation: Each non-claim is a scope rule; none is a theorem.

records.name: Imported 1D Kitaev chain model
records.summary: The spinless p-wave Kitaev chain H = -sum(t c_j^dag c_{j+1} + Delta c_j c_{j+1} + h.c.) - mu sum(c_j^dag c_j - 1/2), its BdG spectrum, the phase region |mu| < 2t with Delta nonzero, and the sweet-spot form H = -i t sum gamma_{2j} gamma_{2j+1} with free edge modes gamma_1, gamma_{2L} are imported models.
records.obligation: No statement that a physical wire realizes this Hamiltonian without disorder or trivial subgap states is made or supported.

records.name: Sweet-spot bonds avoid the edge Majorana indices
records.summary: For every bond (u, v) = (2j, 2j+1) with 1 <= j < L, u and v differ from 1 and from 2L.
records.obligation: Index-level statement only; operator commutation [H, gamma_1] = 0 is the exact instance MAJ-KITAEV-SWEETSPOT-EXACT.

records.name: Exact sweet-spot Kitaev commutators on two modes
records.summary: On the exact Gaussian-rational 2-mode Fock carrier with t = Delta = 1, mu = 0, the Kitaev Hamiltonian is Hermitian, commutes with fermion parity, commutes with gamma_1 and gamma_4, and the bulk invariant is -1.
records.obligation: Fixed L = 2 instance; general L and the BdG spectrum remain imported.

records.name: Imported Ising anyon model and its braiding limits
records.summary: The Ising model {1, sigma, psi} with sigma x sigma = 1 + psi, sigma x psi = sigma, psi x psi = 1 and the R, F data R = e^{-i pi/8} diag(1, i), F = (1/sqrt2)[[1,1],[1,-1]] on the four-sigma fusion space are imported; Ising braiding alone yields only Clifford operations, classically simulable by Gottesman-Knill, so magic-state inputs are required for a complete gate set.
records.obligation: No claim of physical anyon braiding is made; the braid-matrix identities are the open check MAJ-ISING-BRAID-CHECK.

records.name: Exact Q(zeta16) braid identities for the Ising 2x2 matrices
records.summary: For B1 = R and B2 = F R F over Q(zeta16), B1 B2 B1 = B2 B1 B2, F^2 = I and the hexagon equations hold as exact identities.
records.obligation: Run the identities in exact cyclotomic arithmetic; the paper code checks only Yang-Baxter in floating point.

records.name: Exact Yang-Baxter relation for the signed Majorana braid action
records.summary: For 3 to 10 Majoranas the exact signed-permutation exchange action satisfies b_i b_{i+1} b_i = b_{i+1} b_i b_{i+1}, far commutativity, and composition with its inverse gives the identity.
records.obligation: Fixed counts 3..10; this is the Majorana exchange action, not the Ising 2x2 representation.

records.name: Parity observable bookkeeping is algebraic consistency only
records.summary: That a Z2 parity operator squares to I and commutes with an effective Hamiltonian is checked as an algebraic property of declared finite matrices; capacitance shifts C_Q and reflectometry signals stay external models and do not establish protection or coherence.
records.obligation: No experimental readout model is derived.

records.name: Exact parity-sector splitting on the 2-mode Fock carrier
records.summary: On the exact 2-mode Fock carrier the parity operator restricts to 2-dimensional even and odd sectors, and restricting gamma_1 to a sector is refused because it mixes sectors.
records.obligation: Fixed 2-mode instance; the paper code's ParityAlgebraModel check is floating point.

records.name: Sign-reversing pairs cancel in a signed sum
records.summary: For a natural weight w and integer signs with s1 + s2 = 0, w s1 + w s2 = 0 in Int.
records.obligation: Single pair only; no global involution on a configuration space is constructed.

records.name: GIN fermion-recovery routing rule
records.summary: evaluate_gin_fermion_recovery routes an invalid index to ClosureFailure, a valid index with zero uncancelled sign mass to Repair, and positive mass to SplitBrainRefusal.
records.obligation: The three lemmas unfold this rule; the Repair label is a routing tag, not a sign-problem solution.

records.name: Continuous-to-discrete transfer envelope under quasiparticle poisoning
records.summary: For four MZMs under a Lindblad braiding model with gap Delta, length L/xi and poisoning rate Gamma_qp > 0, the trace-norm transfer defect obeys Delta_transfer(T) <= min(1, C_LZ (hbar/(Delta T))^2 + (Delta/hbar) e^{-L/xi} T + 1 - e^{-Gamma_qp T}) for T >> hbar/Delta, and that envelope has a positive minimum.
records.obligation: Derive the envelope from the Lindblad equation; a positive physical lower bound on Delta_transfer needs an independent argument, as the source notes.

records.name: Non-Markovian bosonic-bath transfer envelope
records.summary: For a bath J(w) = 2 pi alpha w_c^{1-s} w^s e^{-w/w_c}, the envelope C_LZ (hbar/(Delta T))^2 + A_s T^p has minimizer T* = (2 C_LZ hbar^2 / (p A_s Delta^2))^{1/(p+2)}, a positive minimum for alpha > 0, and exponent beta = 2/(p+2).
records.obligation: Derive the bath term A_s T^p and p(s) from the spectral density; the calculus minimization of the stated envelope is not written out.

records.name: Multi-terminal cross-junction transfer envelope under disorder
records.summary: For an M-terminal junction (M >= 4) with Delta_eff = Delta_0 (1 - sigma_V/sigma_crit), the transfer envelope adds C(M,2) >= 6 pairwise splitting channels, its minimum rises with sigma_V on (0, sigma_crit), and the gap closes for sigma_V >= sigma_crit.
records.obligation: Derive the envelope and the monotonicity in sigma_V; the gap-degradation law is posited.

records.name: Natural-number positivity lemmas cited for the transfer envelopes
records.summary: Over Nat: products and sums of positive naturals are positive, p > 0 gives p + 2 > 0, p > q gives p + 2 > q + 2, M >= 4 gives M (M - 1) / 2 > 0, and a > b gives a - b > 0.
records.obligation: These lemmas do not bear on any physical envelope; MAJ-C18..C20 stay open.

records.name: Exact rational l1 LP dual lower bounds for Phi1
records.summary: Exact rational l1 linear programming with dual certificates may give certified lower bounds on the F2 coset weight, certifying cosets beyond the search budget where they meet the capped upper bound and reporting the gap otherwise.
records.obligation: No LP relaxation or dual certificate for the F2 coset weight is implemented in this source.

records.name: Evidence adequacy of laboratory measurement maps
records.summary: Whether a declared laboratory protocol's measurement map M separates topological zero modes from trivial Andreev bound states, i.e. whether rho_topo - rho_ABS lies outside ker M.
records.obligation: Requires a declared device model and measurement map; none is supplied.

records.name: Self-consistent Poisson-Schrodinger junction solver
records.summary: A self-consistent 3D Poisson-Schrodinger solver coupling gate geometry, dielectric screening and subband chemical-potential pinning to evaluate phase-boundary shrinkage in multi-terminal junctions.
records.obligation: Listed as the next test; no solver exists in this checkout.

records.name: Canonical anticommutation relations on the exterior Fock space
records.summary: On an admitted N-dimensional complex inner-product space V with orthonormal basis e_i, creation c_i^dagger = e_i wedge - and interior annihilation c_i on the exterior algebra of V (dimension 2^N) satisfy {c_i, c_j} = 0 and {c_i, c_j^dagger} = delta_ij; in particular (c_i)^2 = 0.
records.obligation: Mechanize the CAR identities on the exterior algebra; the statistics choice (exterior versus symmetric algebra) is an admitted postulate, and identifying modes with spin-1/2 particles needs the relativistic spin-statistics theorem, outside this finite setting.

records.name: Jordan-Wigner parity sign of an occupation-basis hop
records.summary: In the increasing occupation ordering on 6 modes, the sign of the hop c_target^dagger c_source on every occupation bitmask equals the product of the Jordan-Wigner parities of the annihilation and the creation step, checked exhaustively over all 2^6 states and ordered mode pairs.
records.obligation: The general Jordan-Wigner bijection c_j = (prod_{k<j} -sigma^z_k) sigma^-_j between spin-1/2 chains and CAR operators is a standard result imported here, not derived or mechanized in this checkout.

records.name: Majorana decomposition, Clifford relations and fermion parity
records.summary: For N CAR modes, gamma_{2j-1} = c_j + c_j^dagger and gamma_{2j} = -i(c_j - c_j^dagger) are self-adjoint with {gamma_a, gamma_b} = 2 delta_ab, generate the Clifford algebra on 2N generators, and P = prod_j (-i gamma_{2j-1} gamma_{2j}) is the fermion parity (-1)^N_op.
records.obligation: Standard algebra imported, not derived here; the trunk mechanizes only the two-generator case (DS-QM212-MAJORANA-PROBLEM). Parity superselection is a physical postulate, not a consequence of the algebra.

records.name: CAR kinematics do not select a fermionic Hamiltonian
records.summary: The CAR constrain the operators c_i, not the Hamiltonian: H = 0, free hopping -t sum c_i^dagger c_j and the Hubbard H(t, U) are distinct Hermitian number-conserving operators on the same CAR Fock space, so a physical Hamiltonian is an added admission (explicit 2-site Hubbard matrix computed by hand).
records.obligation: Hermiticity, number conservation, a locality graph, a one- and two-body truncation and the interaction U remain explicit admissions in every downstream sign record.

records.name: Closed-path series for a signed hopping Hamiltonian
records.summary: For a finite self-adjoint H with H_xx = V_x, H_xy = -a_xy (-1)^{eps_xy} (a_xy > 0, eps symmetric), beta >= 0 and E* >= max V_x, Z = e^{-beta E*} sum_m beta^m/m! sum over closed length-m configuration paths of prod K_{x_{j+1} x_j} with K = E* I - H, and each nonzero closed term has sign (-1)^{sum of eps along the path}.
records.obligation: The sign of a closed term is a property of the supplied magnitudes, parities and representation; vertex sign gauges remove all negative entries exactly when every configuration cycle is even (FSP-SWITCHING-NORMAL-FORM). Trotter slicing and its error are separate.

records.name: Average sign and free-energy gap of a declared representation
records.summary: For a declared path representation with weights W(c), <Sign> = Z / Z_abs with Z = sum sigma(c)|W(c)| and Z_abs = sum |W(c)|; when Z > 0, Delta f := -(1/(beta N)) log <Sign> >= 0, so <Sign> = exp(-beta N Delta f) holds by definition.
records.obligation: Exponential decay in beta N is a hypothesis (Delta f bounded below by a positive constant uniformly in N and beta), not a theorem; Z_abs is an operational absolute ensemble, not in general a physical bosonic system.

records.name: Variance of the Monte Carlo sign estimator
records.summary: For M_s independent samples from |W|/Z_abs, the sign mean has variance (1 - <Sign>^2)/M_s, so relative error epsilon needs M_s >= (1 - <Sign>^2)/(epsilon^2 <Sign>^2); if <Sign> = exp(-beta N Delta f) this is Omega(exp(2 beta N Delta f)).
records.obligation: Correlated Markov-chain samples, observable numerators and the extensive-gap hypothesis need separate treatment; this bound concerns direct reweighting only, not every estimator or representation.

records.name: Representation-dependent negativity on the free triangle
records.summary: For the 3-site spinless triangle, t = 1, U = 0, two fermions, beta = 2 and three Euler slices, the occupation-basis expansion has 27 paths, 6 negative of weight 8/27 and positive weights in {4/9, 1}, so no equal-weight pairing exists there; in the one-body eigenbasis H is diagonal with E in {-1, -1, 2} and Z = 2e^2 + e^-4.
records.obligation: Frustration alone does not imply disjoint weight spectra or hardness (ledger GIN-C4, INV-DISJOINT-SPEC); the general Lean lemma covers only the step from disjoint spectra to no weight-preserving sign-reversing involution.

records.name: Troyer-Wiese worst-case reduction (imported)
records.summary: Troyer-Wiese (2005): the NP-complete decision whether a 3D +-J Ising spin glass has ground energy below a threshold reduces in polynomial time to estimating the thermal energy of the frustrated quantum model -sum J_ij sigma^x_i sigma^x_j at beta J >= N ln 2 + ln(12N); a deterministic polynomial estimator for that family would give P = NP, a randomized one NP subset of BPP.
records.obligation: This is a worst-case statement about a model family under a precision promise; it is not formalized here, is not a reduction to the Hubbard model, and does not make any fixed finite system or every fermionic Hamiltonian intractable.

records.name: Sign-reversing equal-weight involution pairs cancel
records.summary: For any carrier with weights in N and signs +-1, an involution tau with w(tau c) = w(c) and sign(tau c) = -sign(c) has no fixed point and each pair satisfies w(c) sign(c) + w(tau c) sign(tau c) = 0; zero signed sum does not require such a pairing (+2, -1, -1), and a cancelling doublet can carry a nonzero observable numerator.
records.obligation: Summing pairs to get sum_c w(c) sign(c) = 0 on a finite set is a prose orbit-partition step (manuscript Section 4.2), not mechanized; observable numerators need A o tau = A; the involution is sufficient, not necessary (INV-INVOL-CANC).

records.name: GIN equal-weight pairing on the four-site ring fixture
records.summary: For the four-site periodic ring, U = 0, two spin-up fermions, beta = 3/2 and four Euler slices, all 32 negative Euler-transfer paths are matched to disjoint positive paths of exactly equal rational weight within one weight fiber, and a posting-list query over k modes uses k posting-list operations.
records.obligation: Pairing is on exact weight fibers of enumerated paths, not a spectator-preserving symmetry (INV-GIN-PARITY); it does not preserve general observables, and path enumeration grows exponentially. CT-AUX update stability for multi-orbital models has no evidence here.

records.name: Rational cochain quotient normal form
records.summary: For d0 in Q^{m x n} and W = im d0, N_W(x) = x - sum_i x_{p_i} r_i (nonzero RREF rows r_i of d0^T with pivots p_i) is sound, idempotent and complete for x ~ y iff x - y in W, and is independent of the generating matrix; Lean checks the three laws for the fixed integral image span(1, 2) in Z^2.
records.obligation: N_W is not an l1 minimizer (span(1,2), x = (1,0) gives norm 2 versus 1); the quotient norm is a separate exact linear program with a refusal budget (NF-003). A valid YAML contract or routing label is not a normalizer.

records.name: Compact lattice U(1) Wilson action gauge invariance
records.summary: With link phases U_ij = exp(i A_ij) and oriented plaquette products U_p, the Wilson action S = beta_g sum_p (1 - Re U_p) is invariant under local U(1) gauge transformations and nonnegative.
records.obligation: Standard lattice-gauge fact imported, not established in this checkout; the source supplies no fermion-sign consequence for it.

records.name: Wilson-Dirac gamma5-hermiticity and real determinant
records.summary: The Wilson-Dirac operator satisfies gamma5 D_W gamma5 = D_W^dagger, so its nonreal eigenvalues come in conjugate pairs and det D_W is real; for two degenerate flavors det(D_W)^2 >= 0.
records.obligation: A single-flavor det D_W can be negative; the JSONL claim that det D_W is nonnegative is only the two-flavor square. The gamma5 adjoint, reality of det D_W, and the two-flavor square for this operator are not Lean theorems in this checkout. Euclidean Clifford data in dimensions 2 and 4 are checked in Lean. An exact check on one periodic 2x2 lattice, mass -1, U(1), finds det = -3.

records.name: Topological theta term makes lattice weights complex
records.summary: Adding S_theta = i theta Q_top with real lattice charge Q_top multiplies the Boltzmann weight by exp(-i theta Q_top), which is nonreal unless theta Q_top lies in pi Z for every configuration, so positive-weight importance sampling is lost for generic theta != 0.
records.obligation: Severity of the resulting sign problem is phenomenology from the literature; the checkout has no theta-term model.

records.name: Callan-Harvey anomaly inflow on a finite slab lattice
records.summary: Target: on a finite slab lattice the chiral variation of the boundary fermion determinant cancels the bulk Chern-Simons variation. Not established in this checkout. One tested candidate does not realize it, as expected: on open Wilson slabs with U(1) links, the gauge change acts on the Wilson matrix by a diagonal similarity, so the full, interior, boundary Schur and fixed site-matched chiral-block determinants are gauge invariant by construction, while a lifted cup-product CS term whose coefficient is not derived from the fermions changes by 1/32. This is a fixed-basis truncation of a vector-like regulator, not an obstruction to lattice inflow.
records.obligation: Construct a regulated chiral boundary determinant whose projector, basis or measure depends on the gauge field (domain-wall or overlap/Ginsparg-Wilson type), derive from the same fermions the bulk Chern-Simons term they induce, and show that the two gauge variations cancel. The fixed-basis Wilson-slab test cannot register an anomaly, because site-matched fixed bases give similarity-invariant determinants; its bare lifted CS candidate is neither induced by the fermions nor well defined on U(1) links (an integer lift of the same links changes it by 1/8). The continuum Callan-Harvey mechanism remains a literature import.

records.name: SU(2) adjoint fermions have a real determinant
records.summary: For lattice SU(2) with Dirac fermions in the real adjoint representation, an antiunitary symmetry of the Dirac operator makes det D_adj real for every gauge configuration.
records.obligation: For a single Majorana adjoint flavor the measure is a Pfaffian whose sign can change; reality is not positivity. Not established in this checkout.

records.name: Complex quark determinant at real chemical potential
records.summary: For lattice Dirac operators with chemical potential, gamma5 D(mu) gamma5 = D(-mu*)^dagger, hence det D(mu)^* = det D(-mu*); for real mu != 0 this relates D(mu) to D(-mu) only and det D(mu) is in general complex.
records.obligation: Standard identity imported; the checkout has no SU(3) staggered operator and no computation of det D(mu).

records.name: Z3 center projection and baryon triality
records.summary: Claimed: averaging over Z3 center phases cancels the signs of fractional-triality quark paths and leaves color-singlet zero-triality contributions; no model, projection identity or computation for this exists in this checkout.
records.obligation: State the canonical-ensemble center projection as an identity on a declared lattice model and show which signs it removes; ledger GIN-C10 and GIN-C11 withdraw the fixture reading.

records.name: Real determinant at imaginary chemical potential
records.summary: At mu = i mu_I with real mu_I, gamma5 D(i mu_I) gamma5 = D(i mu_I)^dagger, so det D(i mu_I) is real; nonnegativity needs two degenerate flavors (or a staggered operator m + K with K anti-Hermitian, m > 0), and Z(mu_I) has Roberge-Weiss periodicity 2 pi T / 3.
records.obligation: Analytic continuation from imaginary to real mu is an extrapolation, not a sign-free route to real mu; not established in this checkout.

records.name: Lattice Wess-Zumino supercharge algebra
records.summary: Claimed: a finite-lattice 2D N=1 Wess-Zumino model with supercharges obeying {Q_a, Q_b} = 2 delta_ab H, H >= 0 and exact boson-fermion pairing of nonzero levels; no such lattice construction exists in this checkout, and lattice discretizations generally keep at most a subalgebra exact.
records.obligation: Specify the lattice model and which supercharge is exact; prove H = Q^2 or {Q, Q^dagger} on the finite Hilbert space before using pairing.

records.name: Nicolai map sign elimination (unsupported)
records.summary: Claimed: on an off-shell supersymmetric lattice model the map xi = -partial^2 phi + W'(phi) has Jacobian equal to the fermion determinant and turns the partition function into a Gaussian with no sign problem; nothing in this checkout constructs the map or the Jacobian identity.
records.obligation: Give the lattice model, prove det(d xi / d phi) = det D_F, and treat the sign of det D_F and the multiplicity of the map; Nicolai-map results are model specific in the literature.

records.name: Witten index beta-independence under exact supersymmetry
records.summary: On a finite-dimensional graded Hilbert space with an exact supercharge Q and H = {Q, Q^dagger}, positive-energy levels pair bosons with fermions, so W = Tr[(-1)^F exp(-beta H)] = n_B(E=0) - n_F(E=0) for every beta, and unbroken supersymmetry has ground energy 0.
records.obligation: Standard result imported; it presupposes an exact lattice supercharge, which FSP-DERIV-040 leaves open, and gives no sign-free sampling of Z itself.

records.name: Kitaev honeycomb exact Majorana solution
records.summary: Kitaev (2006): in the four-Majorana representation of the honeycomb model, the plaquette fluxes W_p commute with H and with each other, and in each flux sector H is quadratic in the c Majoranas with a static Z2 gauge field (after projection to the physical subspace).
records.obligation: A sign-free sampling claim for this representation is not made or checked here; the gauge projection and flux-sector sum must be kept explicit.

records.name: Laughlin quasihole exchange phase pi/m
records.summary: Arovas-Schrieffer-Wilczek: adiabatic exchange of two quasiholes in the nu = 1/m Laughlin state gives statistical phase theta = pi/m.
records.obligation: No Berry-phase or torus computation is in this checkout; the local module fixes m = 3 and checks numeric constants only (ledger GIN-C16 withdraws its reading).

records.name: Fibonacci anyon fusion and braiding data
records.summary: The Fibonacci category has fusion tau x tau = 1 + tau, quantum dimension d_tau = (1 + sqrt 5)/2 (irrational), F and R matrices solving the pentagon and hexagon equations, and three-anyon braids generate a dense subgroup of SU(2) (Freedman-Larsen-Wang).
records.obligation: The JSONL calls d_tau rational, which is false; the claim that braiding avoids sign degradation has no content here. Exact ribbon data are pinned elsewhere in the trunk (TFQ-0050), not in this package.

records.name: Regge deficit angles and action
records.summary: On a 4D triangulation with squared edge lengths, the deficit angle at a hinge h is epsilon_h = 2 pi - sum of dihedral angles at h and the Regge action is S = sum_h A_h epsilon_h; its convergence to the Einstein-Hilbert action under refinement is a literature result imported here.
records.obligation: Regge calculus carries no fermion-sign content in this package; Lorentzian signature, convergence conditions and any sign consequence need separate evidence (ledger GIN-C13).

records.name: Discrete Wheeler-DeWitt constraint on triangulations
records.summary: Claimed: a discrete Wheeler-DeWitt operator H_perp on spatial triangulations is nonnegative and acts as a projection on diffeomorphism-invariant states; no such operator is constructed here, and the DeWitt supermetric of the continuum constraint is indefinite.
records.obligation: Construct H_perp on a declared finite state space and determine its spectrum; the manuscript separates the constraint H_perp Psi = 0 from thermal Hamiltonians (Section 2.5).

records.name: Pachner-move invariance of a triangulation sum (unsupported)
records.summary: Claimed: a discrete topological partition function on 4D triangulations is invariant under the 1-5, 2-4 and 3-3 Pachner moves; the source names no state-sum model, and the Regge action itself is not Pachner invariant.
records.obligation: Fix a state-sum model (for example a Crane-Yetter type sum) and check its move invariance; nothing here bears on fermion signs.

records.name: CDT causal foliation and positive transfer matrix (unsupported)
records.summary: Claimed: a global proper-time foliation in CDT forbids spatial branching, removes Lorentzian cancellations, yields a sign-free positive transfer matrix and a 4D de Sitter universe; the de Sitter phase is numerical literature and the checkout has no transfer-matrix or positivity computation.
records.obligation: Positivity in CDT uses a Wick rotation of a declared action; derive it for a declared finite model and keep numerical phase results as external evidence.

records.name: Dirac-Kaehler tastes and spinfoam boundary signs (unsupported)
records.summary: Claimed: Dirac-Kaehler fermions on simplicial lattices give 2^(D/2) flavors and EPRL-FK boundary contractions yield nonnegative spin-network weights; the only local content is the count 1+4+6+4+1 = 16 = 4 x 4 in D = 4, and no spinfoam amplitude is evaluated.

records.name: X-cube fracton model ground-state degeneracy
records.summary: Vijay-Haah-Fu (2016): the X-cube model on an Lx x Ly x Lz periodic cubic lattice has pairwise commuting vertex and cube terms and ground-state degeneracy 2^(2Lx + 2Ly + 2Lz - 3).
records.obligation: Imported literature result; the checkout has no X-cube stabilizer computation, and it has no fermion-sign consequence by itself.

records.name: X-cube excitation mobility classes
records.summary: In the X-cube model isolated fractons are immobile, fracton dipoles move within planes (planons) and lineons move only along lattice axes.
records.obligation: The claim that these constraints suppress sign-inducing braids has no evidence here and is left open.

records.name: Hinge-lineon fermion sign elimination (unsupported)
records.summary: Claimed: lineons confined to 1D hinge lines cannot exchange without collision, so their worldlines carry no nontrivial permutations and foliated fracton models are sign free; no model, path expansion or sign computation exists in this checkout.

records.name: Involution-or-NP-hard dichotomy for finite systems (refuted as stated)
records.summary: The claimed dichotomy (each finite quantum system either admits a certified sign-eliminating involution found in polynomial time or is an NP-hard sign obstruction) fails as stated: NP-hardness is a property of input families, the free triangle has no equal-weight involution in its declared basis yet is solved by one-body diagonalization, and zero signed mass need not come from an involution.
records.obligation: The open research content is FSP-EFFICIENT-SAMPLING-OBLIGATIONS: for a stated model family and input encoding, separate exact finite identities, protected sign-free representations, efficient samplers and worst-case hardness.

records.name: Tensor factorization of the dimension-six carrier as C^2 tensor C^3
records.summary: Fix the identification C^6 = C^2 tensor C^3 with product basis |j,k> = |j> tensor |k> for j in {0,1} and k in {0,1,2}; this is a declared choice of tensor factorization of the six-dimensional carrier.
records.obligation: The source statement that every 6x6 operator decomposes into Pauli and Gell-Mann tensor products, and its SU(2)/SU(3) reading, are not checked here; the factorization selects no MUB structure.

records.name: No field of order six, so no finite-field MUB construction at d = 6
records.summary: No finite field has six elements, since finite fields have prime-power order; hence the finite-field Weyl-character construction of d+1 MUBs has no instance at d = 6.
records.obligation: This rules out one construction route only; it gives no upper bound on the number of MUBs in C^6 and does not exclude a complete family produced by another construction.

records.name: Clock and shift operators in dimension six
records.summary: On C^6 with shift X|j> = |j+1 mod 6> and clock Z|j> = w^j |j>, w = exp(2 pi i/6), one has Z X = w X Z, and the 36 operators X^p Z^q are pairwise orthogonal for the trace pairing tr(A* B).
records.obligation: These standard identities are not checked in this checkout for d = 6; the source writes X Z = w Z X, which holds only under the opposite clock convention; no MUB count follows from them.

records.name: Weyl-Heisenberg stabilizer classes over Z_6 and the three-basis claim
records.summary: Claim: maximal commuting classes of the Weyl-Heisenberg group over Z_6 do not partition the 35 non-identity displacement classes and yield at most three MUBs in C^6.
records.obligation: Give the exact stabilizer-class statement with a cited proof or an exact enumeration; even then it bounds only Weyl-Heisenberg constructions, not arbitrary MUBs.

records.name: Quartet existence as a raw complex Hadamard completion problem
records.summary: A quartet of pairwise unbiased orthonormal bases of C^6 exists iff some 6x6 matrix H has a raw quartet: H, U, V with unit-modulus entries, M* M = 6I, and |(A* B)_ij|^2 = 6 for each pair; raw-quartet existence is invariant under row and column permutation-phase equivalence.
records.obligation: Global exclusion still needs complete representative coverage and nonextension for every representative, which no_quartet_of_concrete_representatives takes as hypotheses.

records.name: Explicit three-phase Fourier-Dita matrices are complex Hadamard
records.summary: For unit phases a, b, c the explicit matrix fourierDitaMatrix(a,b,c), built from w = exp(2 pi i/3) blocks with rows signed by a, b, c, has unit-modulus entries and H H* = 6I.
records.obligation: The defect value 4 of F_6, the equivalence F_6 ~ F_2 tensor F_3, the Jaming et al. nonextension theorem for this family, and exhaustion of the Fourier orbit by the displayed matrices are cited or open, not formalized here.

records.name: The displayed matrix labelled Haagerup is complex Hadamard
