records.obligation: The source one-parameter family H6(q) without 2x2 or 3x3 Hadamard sub-blocks is not constructed; matching this matrix to the Haagerup source and to any exclusion theorem is an open step.

records.name: Szollosi two-circulant family: unitarity and deltoid parameter domain
records.summary: For unit phase triples a, b with a0 a2* + a1 a0* + a2 a1* + b0 b2* + b1 b0* + b2 b1* = 0, the block matrix [[A, B], [B*, -A*]] of circulants has H H* = 6I and H/sqrt 6 is unitary with squared entry moduli 1/6; alpha is in both phase-sum images x + y + conj(xy) and -alpha iff some real solution of the six parameter equations has first phase sum alpha.
records.obligation: Transport to a dephased representative, classification of arbitrary CHM(6), the source cusp rank-degeneration claim, and Conjecture 3 (no quartet contains a family member) are not established.

records.name: Two-phase affine ansatz labelled Karlsson is complex Hadamard

records.obligation: No equivalence to the full three-parameter Karlsson family is supplied; the source claim that the CHM(6) moduli space has real dimension at most 4 with a finite chart cover is open.

records.name: The Tao matrix S6 is complex Hadamard

records.obligation: The source claims that S6 is isolated and that the CHM(6) moduli space is disconnected are cited literature facts, not formalized here.

records.name: Dephasing and corner-determinant routing of CHM(6)
records.summary: Every 6x6 complex Hadamard matrix is Hadamard-equivalent to a dephased complex Hadamard matrix D, and D falls into the corner-determinant zero or nonzero case, each assigned a component label.
records.obligation: The labels carry no parameters or family realization; FullModuliClassification follows only from FiveBranchRealizationHypothesis, and the superseded notice withdraws reading this as routing to certified components.

records.name: Deltoid-cover candidate box contains no unbiased basis
records.summary: The deltoid-cover candidate box requires |U_00|^2 >= 81/100, giving margin (81/100 - 1/6)^2 = 37249/90000, while every basis unbiased to the standard basis has |U_00|^2 = 1/6; so the box contains no admissible candidate and its exclusion covers none.
records.obligation: Subdividing the family parameter domain does not enlarge this candidate domain; a valid cover must range over candidates with all squared entry moduli 1/6.

records.name: Szollosi-family quartets as a 618-equation quadratic system
records.summary: For the Szollosi two-circulant family with both additional bases arbitrary, quartet existence (at some and at each fixed admissible parameter) is equivalent to a real solution of 618 rational equations of degree at most two in 440 variables, and every solution lies in the box of radius 1 for phase and raw-basis coordinates and 3 for cross-product coordinates.
records.obligation: Emptiness over all admissible parameters and all third bases (no_quartet_iff_all_varieties_empty) is open; the system covers quartets containing a family member only.

records.name: Gauged 666-equation system and six-chart cover
records.summary: At each admissible Szollosi parameter, quartet existence is equivalent to a solution of the 666-equation system (618 original, 24 column-gauge and 24 derived balance equations) in 440 coordinates, and to such a solution lying in one of six overlapping native candidate charts.
records.obligation: All six charts return UNRESOLVED_BOX in duplicate native runs; none is excluded.

records.name: Exclusion of one Szollosi candidate box via coordinate 368
records.summary: The recorded native candidate box, restricting the six real entries of the first transition row to [-1/2, 1/2], contains no solution of the 666-equation system, because the balance equation forces coordinate 368 into [7/2, 17/2]; the box contains a point with admissible phases (1,-1,1,i).
records.obligation: This excludes one candidate box; it does not exclude all candidates at any family parameter, the six charts, the 56 family cells or the cusp collars.

records.name: Rectangular Krawczyk image and exclusion soundness
records.summary: For finite quadratic coded rows, a box containing the rational centre and any rational preconditioner, every zero in the box lies in the rectangular Krawczyk image, and a successful strict coordinate-separation check excludes all zeros in the box.
records.obligation: Soundness only: no successful check on a quartet domain is supplied, and strict inclusion gives no root conclusion for overdetermined systems.

records.name: Full containing box of the Szollosi system is unresolved
records.summary: On the full containing box of the 618-equation Szollosi system with zero centre and the recorded 28-entry preconditioner, the emitted Jacobian rows and images match the polynomial semantics, every solution is retained, the 144 raw coordinates of the additional bases are not narrowed, no coordinate separates, and every residual interval contains zero.
records.obligation: Status CONTRACTED_UNRESOLVED_BOX and UNRESOLVED_FULL_BOX: no exclusion and no root; generic Rust and JSON decoding is not verified.

records.name: Certified 56-cell membership needs a supplied curvature certificate
records.summary: Certified membership of a point in the stored 56-interval moduli cover is equivalent to geometric membership together with a supplied curvature certificate for its triple.
records.obligation: The 56 stored intervals carry a depth label 64 and positive margins but no contractor execution, per-cell boxes, interval Jacobians or cusp collars; the curvature certificate remains a premise of conjecture3_szollosi_deltoid_closure. The legacy 28-cell, 56-cell, 24-leaf cusp and collar receipts are relabelled NOT_A_CERTIFICATE (literal margins) as of 2026-10-21.

records.name: Common-ray reduction for completing a Hadamard pair
records.summary: For a raw 6x6 complex Hadamard H, H completes to a raw quartet iff two bases of common rays of I and H are raw-unbiased to each other; in particular, if no two common rays z, w have |<z,w>|^2 = 6, then H has no raw quartet.
records.obligation: Exclusion needs the full set of common rays for each H; it is computed only at one special point (MUB6-C41).

records.name: No unbiased pair among represented common rays at one Szollosi point
records.summary: At the Szollosi point (x,y,u,v) = (1,-1,1,i), the 120 real rays given by an exact rational parametrization of unit vectors unbiased to I and S are nonsingular and all 7,140 pairs satisfy ||<z,w>|^2 - 6| > 47/100, so no two represented rays are unbiased.
records.obligation: Completeness of the represented ray set needs an independent bound on the number of complex solutions; the ledger records no replay on 2026-10-16 (python-flint and PARI/GP); one point does not cover the family.

records.name: Projector contract from a supplied complex MUB family
records.summary: From a supplied finite complex MUB family, the matrices P_{b,l} = v_{b,l} v_{b,l}* are self-adjoint, sum to I within each basis, have trace one and rank one, and satisfy tr(P_{b,l} P_{c,k}) = 1/|iota| for distinct bases.
records.obligation: Forward construction only: it does not supply such a family in dimension six or extract one from moments.

records.name: Flat word moments of a supplied MUB family
records.summary: For a supplied MUB family, a state v_{b0,l0} and a distinct basis b1, the complex word-moment matrices of degree one and two are Gram matrices, positive semidefinite, and of equal rank.
records.obligation: Forward theorem for moments induced by a supplied family; no reverse extraction from arbitrary positive flat data.

records.name: Projector extraction from positive flat word moments
records.summary: From normalized word values with positive semidefinite degree-two moments of the same rank as degree one and contextual idempotence equations, one constructs a space of dimension rank M_1, a normalized state and symmetric idempotent actions reproducing all degree-two moments; with contextual same-basis and completeness relations they form orthogonal resolutions of I.
records.obligation: Dimension six, nonzero rank-one outcomes, cross-basis MU conclusions and transport to the coordinate variety are not derived for arbitrary word data.

records.name: Zero-action countermodel to the legacy projector interface
records.summary: The legacy projector-realization interface has a zero-action model on a Boolean carrier for every size label, so the interface-level exclusion predicate is false for every number of bases and dimension.
records.obligation: The interface lacks completeness, rank-one, dimension, linearity and cross-basis MU constraints; exclusions stated over it do not express the physical theorem.

records.name: Common real point from positive flat coordinate moments
records.summary: For a normalized real functional on polynomials whose degree-two coordinate moment matrix is positive semidefinite with rank equal to the degree-one matrix, there is a real point at which every quadratic-span polynomial p with L(p^2) = 0 vanishes.
records.obligation: An extraction theorem; it says nothing about whether such a functional exists for the MUB(6) system.

records.name: Fourth basis iff positive flat compatible moments
records.summary: For a fixed triple T, a fourth basis exists iff some normalized real moment functional has positive semidefinite degree-two moment matrix, equal degree-two and degree-one ranks, and finite relation compatibility with all 180 residuals.
records.obligation: This restates the problem as an equivalent moment question without deciding it; nonflat truncations are not addressed.

records.name: Empty variety forces non-positive flat moments
records.summary: If the fixed-triple variety is empty, every normalized real moment functional with equal degree-two and degree-one ranks and finite relation compatibility has a degree-two moment matrix that is not positive semidefinite.
records.obligation: Emptiness is a hypothesis and is not established for any MU triple.

records.name: First separation replay as the two-mark alphabet
records.summary: In the byte copy of the sealed event semantics, the history of two admitted data, one unary form, one instance on datum 0 and the demand (0,1) replays from the empty regime to a regime in which datum 0 and datum 1 are told apart by a unary instance, giving the alphabet {mark0, mark1}; a fixed instance.
records.obligation: The cost-two minimum (TFQ-0381) and the external definition of separable are not re-proved here; mark0 as <> and mark1 as its first separated successor is a declared labelling.

records.name: Canonical regimes on n marks are pairwise separated
records.summary: For every n, the regime with n data, n-1 unary forms and the instances (i,[i]) is pairwise separated under the unary separation mirror UnarySep, which is decidable with Collapsed and PairwiseSeparated; two admitted marks with no form are collapsed.
records.obligation: UnarySep is a mirror of the hole-only unary case of the Genesis separable, not the external definition; the lift to all contexts including uniform rules is not done.

records.name: Identity convention is a declared input of the computation alphabet
records.summary: Whether an admitted mark is a new state or one internal class with another depends on the identity convention, which is not derived; on a pairwise separated alphabet the opaque and exact-inscription conventions give the same marks, so blank, state and end marks must be admitted as separated marks or the convention declared.
records.obligation: Declare the identity convention before reading any mark of a machine alphabet as a new state; nothing in this chain derives it.

records.name: Words and one-hole rewriting steps
records.summary: Words are lists over the marks; Step R holds between w and w2 when w = u ++ l ++ v and w2 = u ++ r ++ v for a rule l -> r of R; Reach is the reflexive-transitive closure; step_iff_plug reads a step as a rule applied under a one-hole context.
records.obligation: The rule predicate is supplied by the regime; Genesis Step3 is a different relation (COMP-C2e).

records.name: Letter renaming commutes with word steps and reach
records.summary: For every letter map f, a step or reach on words gives a step or reach of the f-image rule predicate on the f-image words; for an injective f a reach of the image comes from a reach of the original (Reach.of_map).
records.obligation: This is the word-side analogue of Genesis Step.rename and Reach.rename, not an instance of them.

records.name: One-hole Genesis contexts are the word contexts
records.summary: A Genesis-style context (a slot tuple with holes, one datum plugged into every hole) has exactly one hole iff it is ofSplit u v for a unique pair of letter lists, and plugging d gives u ++ d :: v; so the one-hole contexts of arity a are the word contexts (u,v) with |u| + |v| = a - 1.
records.obligation: Genesis plugs one datum into every hole while a word rule plugs a word into one hole, which is the wider operation; the sealed regime contexts with forms and rules are not modelled.

records.name: Context counts for small data and arity checked by computation
records.summary: For 2 data and arity 3 there are 19 = 3^3 - 2^3 contexts with a hole and 12 = 3*2^2 with exactly one hole (decide); Rust enumerates n from 0 to 4 and a from 1 to 5, Python n from 0 to 3 and a from 1 to 4, and both match (n+1)^a - n^a and a*n^(a-1).
records.obligation: Finite ranges only; the general formula is the trunk record TFQ-0436.

records.name: Genesis Step3 is not shown to be a word rewriting step
records.summary: Genesis Step3 acts on states of a finite term set, a finite assertion set and two named terms by add-term, add-assertion and identify (a non-injective merge); no word encoding of these states under which each move is a word step is proved or claimed.
records.obligation: Construct a word encoding of Step3 states under which addTerm, addAssertion and identify are word steps, or show that none exists.

records.name: Bounded reachability is decidable on a finite configuration space
records.summary: For k marks, a finite rule list and a length bound L, ReachB is decided by an explicit closure of at most card(wordsLE L) rounds (decideReachB_iff); the configuration space has exactly 1 + k + ... + k^L words (card_wordsLE); Step on a finite rule list is decidable (mem_succList).
records.obligation: This decides rewriting reachability in a declared bound; the decision procedure over all Genesis contexts of the sealed regime asked by TFQ-0497 is not built (COMP-C3c).

records.name: The bounded verdict is sound for the unbounded relation
records.summary: The three-valued verdict returns reachable only for a true Reach, returns unreachable only when the bounded search is closed so no longer path exists, and otherwise returns a witness step that leaves the bound; every Reach is a ReachB for some bound.
records.obligation: Soundness only; the verdict boundExceeded does not decide the unbounded question.

records.name: Unary collapse is decidable; TFQ-0497 stays open
records.summary: The earlier GenesisComputation module decides only unary hole-only separability, collapse and pairwise separation on a finite regime. CampaignGenesisContextDecision now supplies complete finite slot-context decisions with multiple holes, arbitrary finite admitted arities and uniform-rule coverage in the existing Regime. TFQ-0497 remains open for first-count existence, Y-2 history-level necessity and external implementation refinement.
records.obligation: Use the general finite context procedure for the remaining TFQ-0497 history claims under their declared predicates; keep operational refinement separate.

records.name: A right-running machine needs an unbounded supply of fresh blanks
records.summary: The one-state machine that moves right forever reaches words of every length under the TM0 encoding, so its bounded search is closed at no bound and the bounded decider returns boundExceeded at every bound; any regime that reaches arbitrarily long words is closed at no bound.
records.obligation: One concrete machine; the general statement for every general-purpose regime is conditional (COMP-C3e).

records.name: No fixed length bound suffices for a general-purpose regime
records.summary: If the map from an input to its start word were computable and one length bound witnessed every halting start word inside the bound, normal-form reachability would be decidable, contradicting nfReach_not_computable.
records.obligation: Prove startWord_computable (COMP-C7c) and state the uniform version in Lean.

records.name: Genesis stepE has no cap on admission
records.summary: In the byte copy of stepE, k copies of admitDatum replay to data = base.data + k, for every n a history reaches at least n data, and no event lowers the number of data; unbounded admission is permitted by the event semantics.
records.obligation: This is a statement about the copied stepE; every admitDatum is a host event and nothing here generates them.

records.name: Unbounded admission of fresh blank marks is a declared import
records.summary: A general-purpose rewriting regime needs words of unbounded length, which in Genesis terms is unbounded admission of fresh marks; stepE permits it but every admitDatum is a host event, closed Genesis saturates (TFQ-0451, TFQ-0487), TFQ-0482 gives unbounded sequence length over bounded state and not unbounded space, and no endogenous generator exists (TFQ-0504).
records.obligation: Derive an endogenous source of unboundedly many admitted data (TFQ-0504) or keep the supply as a recorded host input.

records.name: Supply growth under demand accounting
records.summary: If in s_next = s - d + b with d_n <= s_n every round has strictly more births than discharges, then the active count is at least s_0 + n after n rounds; the births are an input.
records.obligation: Genesis does not derive the births; this is arithmetic on the accounting identity.

records.name: Turing machine steps are rewrite steps, in both directions
records.summary: For a Mathlib TM0 machine encoded on configuration words lend, left cells, q, a, right cells, rend, a machine step from a represented configuration is matched by a rewrite step to a word representing the next configuration, and every rewrite step of a represented word is the machine step; a word represents at most one configuration.
records.obligation: Machines in the TM0 form only (one write or one move per transition); representations allow blank padding at the far ends; the end rules write a fresh blank, the only place where words grow.

records.name: Reach of represented words is Reaches of the machine, and halting is an irreducible word
records.summary: Forward and backward simulation extend to the closures, and the machine halts from c iff some word reachable from a word representing c is irreducible.
records.obligation: Existential in the target word because a configuration has many padded representations.

records.name: Mark budget and finite rule list of an encoded machine
records.summary: A machine with tape alphabet G and state type L uses |G| + |L| + 2 marks, all of which must be admitted and separated; for finite G and L the rule set is the finite list ruleList M and the bounded decider of C3 applies to it.
records.obligation: The enumeration of marks by an equivalence with Fin is a declared choice.

records.name: Small machines checked by exact computation
records.summary: Rust: a binary incrementer on inputs 0 to 40 with 0 to 2 padding cells (steps 2c+1, value n+1), the two-state busy beaver in the TM0 form (12 steps, 4 ones), step simulation on all 3150 small configurations of that machine; Python: all 6561 two-state two-symbol TM0 machines for 20 steps from the blank tape with a different tape representation; Lean: one write-and-halt machine.
records.obligation: Finite instances; they are not a proof for other machines.

records.name: One fixed code evaluates every code
records.summary: There is a fixed Nat.Partrec.Code u with eval u (pair (encode c) n) = eval c n for all codes c and inputs n, and a fixed ToPartrec code computing the same function on one natural number.
records.obligation: Imported infrastructure is cited, not re-derived; the codes are existence statements chosen by Classical.choose.

records.name: The fixed TM2 machine computes Code.eval in output form
records.summary: The fixed TM2 machine PartrecToTM2.tr, started on init of the fixed code and the paired input, evaluates to halt applied to the value of Code.eval c n exactly when that value is defined.
records.obligation: TM2 level only; the corresponding output form at the TM0 level is open (COMP-C6e).

records.name: The fixed composite TM0 machine halts iff the evaluation halts
records.summary: For the fixed TM0 machine M0 = TM1to0.tr (TM2to1.tr PartrecToTM2.tr) and the explicit initial configurations initCfg0, M0 halts from initCfg0 (pair (encode c) n) iff Code.eval c n is defined.
records.obligation: Halting form only; the TM0 output form is open (COMP-C6e).

records.name: The composite machine uses a finite set of marks
records.summary: Every word reachable from a start word of the fixed rewriting regime has its marks in the finite set markSet: two end markers, the 1250 tape marks of Bool x (K -> Option G), and the state marks of the finite set S0 given by the Mathlib tr_supports chain.
records.obligation: The size of S0 is not computed and the machine is not claimed small.

records.name: Output form of the composite TM0 machine
records.summary: The tape of the halting TM0 configuration of M0 from initCfg0 should read the value of Code.eval c n; Mathlib gives this only existentially through TM2to1.tr_eval and is not composed here.
records.obligation: Prove v in Code.eval c n iff M0 halts from initCfg0 with the encoded v on its output tape.

records.name: Halting of the fixed machine on the start family is not computable
records.summary: For each n, the predicate c -> M0 halts from initCfg0 (pair (encode c) n) is not a computable predicate of the code c.
records.obligation: Imports the halting problem from Mathlib.

records.name: Normal-form reachability of the fixed regime is not computable
records.summary: For the fixed rewriting regime Rules M0 and its explicit family of start words, the predicate that the start word of the input reaches an irreducible word is not computable, as a predicate of the code or of the natural number input.
records.obligation: The statement is about the family startWord; that the input-to-start-word map is computable is not proved (COMP-C7c).

records.name: Reduction over encoded rewriting instances is conditional
records.summary: If the mark type has a Primcodable structure and startWord is computable, the normal-form reachability problem on words of the fixed regime is not a computable predicate.
records.obligation: Prove startWord_computable: a Primcodable structure on a mark type containing the infinite state type and a computability proof for the paired-input encoding.

records.name: Reach to a fixed target word is undecidable
records.summary: Adding erasing rules so that every halting word reduces to one fixed word should make Reach to that fixed word undecidable; this is not proved here.
records.obligation: Prove Reach R0 prime (startWord x) target iff (univFun x).Dom for the extended rule set R0 prime.

records.name: Injective binary coding of any finite alphabet with a decoder
records.summary: For any finite alphabet, the letter-by-letter fixed-width binary code of width clog 2 |alphabet| + 1 is an injective monoid homomorphism on words with the explicit decoder decodeWord (decode_encode), and the same holds with the two separated marks as the target alphabet.
records.obligation: A code is not an isomorphism of free monoids; no claim that a machine over the coded alphabet simulates a machine over the original (Mathlib TM1to1 is not used).

records.name: No smallest general-purpose machine is claimed
records.summary: Two separated marks code the words of any finite alphabet and a blank is a third symbol, but the composite machine M0 is not minimal and no smallest general-purpose machine is claimed; small-machine records are literature only.
records.obligation: State and prove in Lean the simulation of a machine over the coded alphabet by a machine over the two marks and a blank before any minimality statement.

records.name: Does the obstruction a quantum computation generates limit its own ability to finish reliably
records.summary: Every step of a noisy quantum computation, syndrome extraction and repair included, adds residual, and repair consumes capacity while adding residual of its own; the question is whether this makes reliable completion a self-referential no-go or a threshold condition that holds only under named resource assumptions (fresh supply, net-efficient repair, bounded overhead growth, physical error below threshold).
records.obligation: The finite model answers the question as a threshold condition (QCV-Q1 to QCV-Q6); whether any physical system meets the named assumptions is not derived and no verdict on physical viability is given.

records.name: Finite model of per-step residual with repair that generates residual of its own
records.summary: Backlog q(t+1) = max(0, q(t) + lam + g*mu - mu) in units of the Phi_1 repair cost, where lam is the residual generated per round by the computation, mu = kappa*r the repair rate from r fresh ancillas per round at kappa units each, and g the residual generated per unit of repair; with g = 0 this is the DS-QM101 queue; a distance-three level with a fault locations has constant c = a(a-1)/2.
records.obligation: lam, g, kappa and r are declared inputs; no value is derived or measured for any code, and Phi_1 of a residual is not computed here.

records.name: Backlog is bounded exactly when the net repair rate covers generation; unit-gain repair never bounds it
records.summary: In the QCV-Q1 model with q0 >= 0, the backlog is bounded iff lam <= (1-g)*mu; for g >= 1 and lam > 0 no mu >= 0 bounds it; for g < 1 and mu = kappa*r, with kappa > 0, it is bounded iff r >= lam/((1-g)*kappa); with r = 0 and lam > 0 it equals q0 + t*lam.
records.obligation: A statement inside the declared model; it does not say any code has g < 1 or that any supply r is available.

records.name: Without a squaring repair step the error never contracts, and added repair locations lower the certified threshold
records.summary: The union-bound recurrence p(k+1) = a*p(k) with a >= 1 and p(0) > 0 does not tend to zero; for 2 <= a <= b fault locations the certified threshold 1/pairCount(b) is at most 1/pairCount(a).
records.obligation: The location counts are declared; nothing here says how many repair locations a physical code needs.

records.name: Threshold theorem for concatenated codes (literature)
records.summary: The fault-tolerance threshold theorems (Shor 1996; Aharonov and Ben-Or 1997; Kitaev 1997; Knill, Laflamme and Zurek 1998; Aliferis, Gottesman and Preskill 2006) are cited under each theorem's own noise, locality and overhead hypotheses; they are not re-proved.
records.obligation: Exact constants and noise hypotheses of each theorem are not reproduced; the finite recurrence in QCV-Q2 is the only part checked.

records.name: Concatenation recurrence p(k+1) = c*p(k)^2: exact closed form and threshold dichotomy over the rationals
records.summary: For the recurrence p(k+1) = c*p(k)^2 over Q, c*p(k) = (c*p(0))^(2^k); for c > 0 and p(0) >= 0: if c*p(0) < 1 then p(k) tends to zero with c*p(k) <= (c*p(0))^(k+1) and, for c*p(0) <= 1/2, p(k) <= (1/2)^(2^k)/c; if c*p(0) = 1 then p(k) = 1/c for all k; if c*p(0) > 1 then p(k) diverges; so p(k) tends to zero iff p(0) < 1/c.
records.obligation: The recurrence is the hypothesis; no noise model is shown to obey it and no constant c is computed for any code.

records.name: Exact criterion on a level-dependent overhead for the existence of a threshold region
records.summary: For p(k+1) = c(k)*p(k)^2 with c(k) >= 0, p(k) = p(0)^(2^k)*amp(k) with amp(0) = 1, amp(k+1) = c(k)*amp(k)^2, and some p(0) > 0 has p(k) tending to zero iff some M > 0 has amp(k) <= M^(2^k) for all k; the criterion holds for c(k) <= C, for c(k) <= A*B^(k+1) with A, B >= 1, for c(k) = (k+1)^2, and for c(k) <= a*b^N(k) with block size N(k+1) <= s*N(k), s < 2; it fails for c(k) >= a*b^(2^k) with a > 0, b > 1, and for c(k) >= a*b^N(k) with 2^k <= N(k), b > 1, where no positive p(0) has p(k) tending to zero.
records.obligation: The families are exact illustrations of the criterion, not claims that any physical overhead has such a form; correlated-noise strength as an exponential of block size is a declared toy.

records.name: Limitations of noisy reversible computation without fresh bits (literature)
records.summary: Aharonov, Ben-Or, Impagliazzo and Nisan (1996) show that noisy reversible or quantum computation with no supply of fresh low-entropy bits cannot preserve its input beyond a short depth; the result is cited, not re-proved or imported as a proof here.
records.obligation: The exact statement and its noise model are in the cited paper; QCV-Q4 establishes a finite exact analogue for global depolarizing noise only.

records.name: Trace distance of two noisy unitary histories without fresh resources decays by the product of one minus the noise rates
records.summary: For complex matrices of any size d and the variational trace norm tn(X) = sup over unitaries U of |tr(UX)|, the global depolarizing channel satisfies tn(Delta_p(rho) - Delta_p(sigma)) = (1-p)*tn(rho - sigma) for equal-trace rho, sigma and p <= 1; along any history of unitaries V(i) with depolarizing rates p(i) in [0,1], tn(run rho - run sigma) = (product of (1-p(i)))*tn(rho - sigma), which is at most (1-p)^t*tn(rho - sigma) when every p(i) >= p, and (1-p)^t <= 1/(1+p*t).
records.obligation: The trace norm is the variational form, whose equality with the sum of singular values is cited; the noise is global depolarizing with a declared rate per step, not independent per-qubit noise, and the statement is about histories without fresh resets.

records.name: Exact qubit form: squared Bloch distance of two noisy histories contracts by the product of squared factors
records.summary: For rational Bloch vectors, noisy steps r -> (1-p)*R*r with rational rotations R (R^T R = 1) give sqDist(run r, run s) = (product of (1-p(i))^2)*sqDist(r, s), at most ((1-p)^2)^t*sqDist(r, s) when every p(i) in [p,1]; and (v.sigma)^2 = (v.v)*1 over the complex numbers, so the difference of two qubit states has both singular values |r-s|/2.
records.obligation: The identification of the qubit trace norm with the Bloch distance uses the cited eigenvalue fact; Python and Rust replays are exact on declared instances only.

records.name: Conditional viability: explicit logical failure bound under fresh supply, net-efficient repair and bounded overhead
records.summary: If g < 1, kappa > 0, r >= lam/((1-g)*kappa), c(k) <= C, max(C,1)*p(0) < 1 and the level errors p(k) >= 0 obey p(k+1) <= c(k)*p(k)^2 whenever the backlog is bounded, then the backlog is bounded and for every L >= 0 and epsilon > 0 some level k has L*p(k) <= epsilon; with max(C,1)*p(0) <= 1/2 any k with L <= epsilon*max(C,1)*2^(2^k) works.
records.obligation: The noise recurrence is a hypothesis: independence or locality of noise, fresh ancillas, fast classical control and bounded overhead are not shown for any device; the hypotheses are only shown jointly satisfiable on declared toy numbers.

records.name: Inside the model, viability holds exactly when the fresh supply reaches threshold and the overhead means are bounded
records.summary: For g < 1, kappa > 0 and c(k) >= 0, the backlog is bounded and some positive physical rate has p(k) tending to zero iff r >= lam/((1-g)*kappa) and some M > 0 has amp(k) <= M^(2^k); with no supply the backlog is unbounded, with g >= 1 it is unbounded for every supply, and a tight profile p(k+1) >= c(k)*p(k)^2 with c(k) >= a*b^(2^k), b > 1, p(0) > 0 does not tend to zero.
records.obligation: A statement about the declared model: a failed requirement shows the certificate is empty, not that a physical machine fails.

records.name: Whether a physical system meets the conditional viability hypotheses is not derived
records.summary: Whether any physical system has noise obeying the recurrence with level-bounded overhead, a fresh ancilla supply at rate r >= lam/((1-g)*kappa) and fast classical control is not established here, in either direction; the rate comparison mu_repair >= lambda_proj at scale stays open.
records.obligation: A named packet (code family, noise hypothesis, repair capacity, residual quotient) and a locality bound would be needed before any verdict; no claim about physical viability is made.

records.name: Shared structure with the Turing-completeness branch: unbounded computation needs an unbounded supply of fresh distinguished marks
records.summary: A fresh-mark supply is a stream of distinguished marks each usable once; a process consuming at least rmin > 0 marks per round completes at most B/rmin rounds from a total supply B, and a positive per-round consumption exhausts every finite supply; reliable quantum computation of unbounded length (QCV-Q1B, QCV-Q4) and Turing-complete computation in the parallel UTM branch each need such an unbounded supply.
records.obligation: A bridge definition only: no common theorem is proved, no map between the entropy-sink supply and the blank-tape supply of the UTM branch is defined, and that branch is not part of this checkout.

records.name: Read token, halt outcome and terminal policy are separate carriers in a two-presentation tape-control model
records.summary: On the fixed carrier of two halting presentations that differ only in the scanned cell (blank or marked), a control-only report does not determine the supplied content contract, an unread report does not determine it either, one read token admits two supplied semantic adapters, and one halt outcome admits two supplied terminal policies.
records.obligation: State the same four facts for a general tape alphabet and head position; the content contract is chosen to separate the two presentations, so the result exhibits a split fiber and does not derive one.

records.name: Four-configuration transition table: one supplied contract preserved, one fails on a countertrace
records.summary: In a table over the four configurations running-blank, running-marked, halted-blank and halted-marked that exposes advance, stay and halt, the supplied clean-terminal contract is preserved, the supplied marked-cell contract fails from running-marked, the identity report is adequate for the marked-cell contract, and the control-only report is not.
records.obligation: Replace the enumerated carrier by an actual tape and head, and replace the contracts, which were written to produce the countertrace, by contracts stated independently of the table.

records.name: Direct finite-rule machine with total tape, first-match lookup and fuel-bounded evaluation
records.summary: A machine is a designated halt state with an ordered finite rule list over natural-number states, the symbols blank and marked, and the moves left, right and stay; a step returns halted exactly when the state is the halt state, stuck when no rule matches, and otherwise applies the first matching rule; execute iterates at most the given fuel and returns halted, stuck or fuel exhausted with the last configuration.
records.obligation: Relate the model to Mathlib Turing.TM0 by restricting initial tapes to finite support, splitting write-and-move rules into two steps and merging halted with stuck, then prove step simulation; no universality, extensional property or reduction is established here.

records.name: Fuel exhaustion is a typed bounded-run outcome and is not a non-halting verdict
records.summary: A bounded evaluator has three terminal outcomes, halted, stuck and fuel exhausted; the fuel-exhausted outcome records only that the budget ended and is never read as divergence, and a looping fixture exhausts a budget of one step without any claim about whether it halts.
records.obligation: Apply the same three-way typing to the declared-bound runs of the Genesis continuation: a run stopped at the guard or the bound stays unresolved, neither closed nor diverging, until a longer run or a proof decides it.

records.name: Finite natural-number token code for finite-rule machines with a decoder-after-encoder round trip
records.summary: For every finite-rule machine, decoding the token list that encodes it (the halt-state token followed by five-token frames of state, scanned tag, next state, written tag and move tag) returns that machine, and the all-consuming decoder returns none on the empty list, a truncated frame, an invalid symbol tag and an invalid move tag in the four named fixtures.
records.obligation: No converse (encoding after decoding), no source-byte format, no configuration or input encoding and no agreement between parsed code and execution is established; the token alphabet is the natural numbers, so passing to the two-symbol tape alphabet needs a prefix-code argument, since free monoids on alphabets of different sizes are not isomorphic.

records.name: Planned length-delimited request grammar and result-level agreement with the bounded evaluator
records.summary: The update packet plans a request code made of a fuel token, a machine-code length, one machine segment and an input word, whose code-level evaluator decodes the request and calls the bounded evaluator on the declared initial input, with seven named target theorems.
records.obligation: Write the module and prove the request round trip and the result-level agreement; configuration snapshots and step-by-step trace agreement remain separate obligations.

records.name: A no-decider boundary transports through a validity-preserving reduction and a closed decision class
records.summary: If a map from a source predicate into proposal validity preserves the predicate exactly, and the allowed proposal deciders are closed under precomposition with that map, then a source predicate with no allowed total decider gives a proposal predicate with no allowed total decider.
records.obligation: Instantiate the allowed classes with ComputablePred on a code type, take the halting problem as the source predicate and prove closure under the reduction; the declaration supplies none of the three.

records.name: Under a no-total-decider premise no terminalizer is closed, two-sided sound and in the allowed class
records.summary: Given an allowed class with no total decider for a validity predicate, no terminalizer whose authorized bit lies in the class is both acceptance-sound and acceptance-complete, and none is acceptance-sound, rejection-sound and never unresolved; a two-valued Boolean fixture is closed, sound and complete.
records.obligation: The no-total-decider premise and the class membership of the acceptance bit are hypotheses that no program carrier supplies yet; the result does not say that every terminalizer must return unresolved, and it uses three terminal values where TFQ-0330 names five.

records.name: A program carrier is admitted for an undecidability claim only with eight frozen fields
records.summary: A program carrier is admitted for a global undecidability claim only when syntax and encodings, execution semantics, a universality witness, an extensional property, positive and negative nontriviality witnesses, an effective reduction, the split between adequacy and authorization, and replay closure are all frozen in one record.
records.obligation: None of the eight fields is closed by the source: DTM0 and DTM1 are partial on syntax, execution and replay only, and the candidate inventory records admission as open.

records.name: Rice theorem imported for the programs of a Turing-complete language
records.summary: No total computable procedure is sound and complete for a nontrivial extensional property of the programs of a Turing-complete language (Rice 1953); the source cites the theorem with its hypotheses and does not formalize it.
records.obligation: State a local theorem that instantiates Mathlib ComputablePred.rice₂ for the chosen code language, with the semantic property and both nontriviality witnesses named, and bind it to the class-relative transport.

records.name: Global computability lift for an admitted carrier and a nontrivial extensional property
records.summary: For an admitted program carrier and a nontrivial extensional property, a total computable sound and complete authorizer would decide that property; the lift is a stated target in the source and has no local theorem.
records.obligation: Choose the carrier, define the property by program behavior, give the satisfying and failing programs, prove the many-one reduction and the closure of the decision class, and cite rice₂ and halting_problem.

records.name: Frozen blind-derivation protocol for a run from Primitive Difference toward computation
records.summary: A derivation run toward computation is a proposal source: its prompt, model, tools, repository state, available context and outputs are frozen, every notion is labeled input, definition, theorem, example or open assumption, each lift carries a positive witness and a failed-descent control, and literature comparison happens only after sealing; isolation records provenance and does not show novelty or validity.
records.obligation: Apply the protocol to the Genesis to computability derivation and keep recovered material out of any run meant to be blind until that run is sealed.

records.name: DTM0 finite-rule machine with total integer tape and fuel-bounded evaluator
records.summary: A DTM0 machine is a designated halt state with a finite, left-biased list of rows (state, scanned symbol, next state, written symbol, move) over the two-symbol alphabet blank and marked; a configuration is a state, an integer head and a total tape Int to symbol; execute runs at most the stated fuel and returns halted, stuck or fuelExhausted.
records.obligation: The definition carries no input encoding, no unbounded-run semantics, no halting predicate and no comparison with Mathlib Turing.TM0; fuel exhaustion is a bounded-evaluator result and not non-halting.

records.name: DTM0 step reports halted exactly in the designated halt state
records.summary: For every DTM0 machine and configuration, step returns halted exactly when the configuration's state equals the machine's halt state, and execute then returns halted at every fuel budget.
records.obligation: This fixes what a declared halt means in DTM0; it is not a statement about halting of runs and selects no terminal policy.

records.name: DTM0 write-and-halt, stuck and self-loop fixtures
records.summary: On the three named fixtures, writeAndHaltMachine writes a mark and reaches its halt state in one transition, the empty-rule machine is stuck at its first step, and the one-row self-loop machine returns fuelExhausted with the looped configuration after one unit of fuel.
records.obligation: The self-loop result is exhaustion of one unit of fuel; no theorem says the loop never halts, and no fixture exceeds three rows.

records.name: DTM1 List Nat token grammar for DTM0 machines
records.summary: A machine code is the halt-state token followed by complete five-token frames (state, scanned tag, next state, written tag, move tag) with tags 0 and 1 for symbols and 0, 1, 2 for moves; decodeMachine consumes the whole list and returns none on an empty list, a truncated frame or an invalid tag.
records.obligation: Tokens are natural numbers, not bytes; there is no configuration or input encoding and no parser-to-execution agreement.

records.name: DTM1 decode after encode recovers every DTM0 machine
records.summary: For every DTM0 machine m, decodeMachine (encodeMachine m) = some m, supported by the tag round trips decodeTapeSymbol_encodeTapeSymbol and decodeMove_encodeMove and the rule-list round trip decodeRules_encodeRules.
records.obligation: Only decode after encode is stated; injectivity of decode on arbitrary lists and encode after decode are not stated.

records.name: DTM1 rejects empty, truncated and invalid-tag codes
records.summary: decodeMachine returns none on the four named lists [], [0,0,0,1], [0,0,2,1,0,0] and [0,0,0,1,0,3].
records.obligation: Four named inputs only; no theorem characterizes the full domain of decodeMachine.

records.name: A constant receipt cannot decide a one-bit packet contract
records.summary: For the one-bit Packet type with validity equal to its bit, no function from Unit to Bool satisfies authorize (receipt p) = valid p for all p, while the identity report admits such a function.
records.obligation: A toy instance of the split-fibre obstruction; it says nothing about receipts in general.

records.name: Class-relative transport of a no-total-decider premise through a reduction
records.summary: Given a map from source instances to proposals that preserves the source predicate as proposal validity, and closure of the allowed proposal deciders under precomposition with that map, a source predicate with no allowed total decider yields a proposal validity predicate with no allowed total decider.
records.obligation: The allowed classes and the source no-decider premise are supplied; no computability class, halting-style source theorem or Rice reduction is instantiated.

records.name: Class-relative transport instantiated with Mathlib computability for halting
records.summary: With Computable as the allowed class on both sides, a source predicate with no computable total decider and a computable validity-preserving map give proposal validity with no computable total decider; for the source predicate that program c halts on input n this is Mathlib's ComputablePred.halting_problem.
records.obligation: Halting is the only source predicate instantiated; no Rice instance, no extensional property of encoded DTM0 programs and no computable reduction from DTM0 to Nat.Partrec.Code is given.

records.name: An acceptance-sound and acceptance-complete terminalizer yields a total decider
records.summary: For a terminalizer into authorized, rejected, unresolved that is acceptance-sound and acceptance-complete for a validity predicate, the Boolean that is true exactly on authorized decides the predicate; if that Boolean lies in an allowed class with no total decider, the terminalizer cannot be both.
records.obligation: The no-total-decider premise and the membership of the acceptance bit in the allowed class are hypotheses; neither is discharged.

records.name: A rejection-sound terminalizer with no unresolved case is acceptance-complete
records.summary: If a terminalizer never rejects a valid proposal and never returns unresolved, every valid proposal is authorized; with an allowed acceptance bit and no allowed total decider, acceptance-soundness, rejection-soundness and closure cannot all hold.
records.obligation: The result leaves three options (an unsound acceptance, an unsound rejection, or an unresolved case) and does not say any of them must occur for a particular predicate.

records.name: A closed two-sided sound terminalizer exists for the Bool predicate
records.summary: On Bool with validity equal to the bit, the terminalizer sending true to authorized and false to rejected is acceptance-sound, acceptance-complete, rejection-sound and closed.
records.obligation: A decidable one-bit predicate only; it shows closed terminalization is not forbidden without a no-decider premise.

records.name: Control-only and unread reports cannot decide the tape-control content contract
records.summary: In the tape-control model with cells blank and marked and outcomes advance, stay, halt, no function of the control outcome and no function of the always-unread report equals contentContract on every presentation, and the read token blank is given opposite verdicts by the two supplied semantic adapters.
records.obligation: The contract and adapters are supplied examples; the model is not the full Turing-machine model.

records.name: A syntactic halt or verified outcome does not select a terminal policy
records.summary: In the DTM0 model, the tape-control model and the replay model, a halted or verified outcome receives different terminal values from two supplied policies: acceptHalted versus leaveAllOpen, acceptHalt versus rejectAll, and authorizeOnVerified versus leaveVerifiedOpen.
records.obligation: Existence of two policies only; no policy is selected or justified.

records.name: Four-configuration table: one preserved contract and one violated contract
records.summary: The four-configuration transition table maps every configuration to one that cleanTerminalContract accepts, so it preserves that contract, and it does not preserve markedCellContract because runningMarked is accepted while its successor runningBlank is not.
records.obligation: Two supplied Boolean contracts on one finite table; nothing is said about transition systems in general.

records.name: Full-configuration report is adequate for the marked-cell contract; the control report is not
records.summary: On the four configurations the identity report is adequate for markedCellContract, whereas the control-outcome report is not, because haltedBlank and haltedMarked both report stay and the contract separates them, so no function of the control outcome decides the contract.
records.obligation: A finite adequacy example; whether any report is adequate for a semantic property of arbitrary programs is not addressed.

records.name: Replay succeeds only on the submission bound in the receipt
records.summary: In the finite structural replay model, if replay of a receipt on an observed submission returns replayed with some outcome, then the observed submission equals the submission bound in the receipt.
records.obligation: Equality is structural equality of a finite record, not a digest; verifier soundness and custody are not modelled.

records.name: Finite replay model rejects self-pass and substituted checker, contract and schema
records.summary: Under authorizeTrueRoot, verify returns contractRejected for the invalid submission that sets selfPass, returns bindingRejected for the checker, contract-version and schema-version substitutions, issues a receipt that replays the valid submission as verified, and rejects the invalid payload as a substitution.
records.obligation: Six rfl facts on five named submissions; the model does not prove that every substitution is caught.

records.name: Site labels: co-location is enough and separation is not
records.summary: For the presentation with identity report and equal source and evaluator sites, a report-only authorization exists; for the presentation with a Unit report and distinct sites, none exists.
records.obligation: Site is an unused finite label; the statement carries no custody, security or independence content.

records.name: Two authorization extensions over one Bool primitive-difference analogue
records.summary: Over the minimal Bool analogue of a primitive difference with two unequal marks, identityExtension and rejectingExtension give different validity and terminal values at the same carrier point.
records.obligation: The analogue is not the J011 interface and no naturality statement about all primitive differences follows.

records.name: Primitive-difference quotient report cannot decide a ZeroRel-splitting validity
records.summary: For a primitive difference P and a Bool validity that differs on some ZeroRel P class, no function on the canonical quotient report pdProj P agrees with validity everywhere; a ZeroRel-constant validity has a quotient decision.
records.obligation: Not built here: the file imports J011_minimal_publication, whose source is absent from this repository, so the recorded proof is unreplayed.

records.name: SHA-256 replay packet for the four-configuration table (Python port)
records.summary: A manifest binding eight artifacts by SHA-256 together with a four-row transition proposal, a contract and a leave-open policy verifies under the Python port; it finds the clean-terminal contract preserved, the marked-cell contract violated at runningMarked and haltedMarked, the control-outcome report inadequate (haltedBlank and haltedMarked share stay), the route open_due_to_inadequate_report and the terminal open, and refuses 21 tamper mutations.
records.obligation: Evaluator correspondence to the Lean model, SHA-256 collision resistance, runtime integrity and custody remain assumptions; the PowerShell runtime pin is not reproduced and the formal replay uses Lean v4.35.0 instead of the recorded v4.32.2.

records.name: No computability carrier is admitted for the authorization lift
records.summary: The recovered candidate record stays globally open: for AIT-DTM0 only syntax, execution semantics, adequacy and replay closure are partial and universality, extensionality, nontriviality and effective reduction are open, and PO-022, PO-023 and AIT-PACKET4 are open; the validator refuses any selection or admission.
records.obligation: A carrier with syntax, execution, simulation, an extensional property with encoded witnesses, an effective reduction and a replay boundary must be frozen before any Rice-style claim.

records.name: Rice, Goedel and the LLM corollary are not formalized in the recovered files
records.summary: No recovered declaration states Rice's theorem, a halting-problem reduction, Goedel's second incompleteness theorem or the LLM corollary; the only link toward them is the class-relative transport with a supplied no-decider premise, which the recovery-time MathlibBridge file instantiates for halting only.
records.obligation: Instantiate the transport for a nontrivial extensional property of encoded programs with Mathlib's ComputablePred.rice and a computable reduction from the DTM0 carrier before any such claim.

records.name: DTM0 is not shown Turing-complete and has no universality theorem
records.summary: DTM0 has no simulation theorem, no machine that runs encoded machines, no input or configuration encoding, no parser-to-execution agreement and no equivalence with Mathlib's Turing.TM0 or with Nat.Partrec.Code; its fuel-bounded evaluator decides only bounded runs.
records.obligation: A faithful comparison needs a finite-support tape restriction, the stay move split into Mathlib's move-or-write statements, and a halting predicate such as exists fuel with execute returning halted.
